skills.title: Name faces, edges and corners on a solid shape
Count faces, edges and corners of a cube and a cuboid, including the hidden ones
Count faces and corners of other solids such as a square pyramid

expectations: A face is a flat surface, an edge is a line where two faces meet, a corner is a point where edges meet
A picture shows only some faces; the hidden back, bottom and far-side faces must be counted too
A cube and a cuboid both have 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 corners, even though a cuboid's faces are not all the same size
Counting in pairs or in an order (top-bottom, front-back, left-right) stops us missing or double-counting

misconceptions.belief: Counts only the faces or edges that can be seen in a picture
signs: Says a dice has 3 faces when looking at its picture
Counts 9 edges on a drawn cube
Never mentions the bottom or the back of a box

diagnostic.prompt_en: Look at a picture of a dice. You can see 3 faces. How many faces does the dice have in all?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Dice ki picture dekho. Tumhe 3 faces dikh rahe hain. Poore dice mein total kitne faces hain?

remediation.representation: A real box or an on-screen rotatable cube with each face a different colour
remediation.moveShape: Child predicts the count from the picture, then turns the solid face by face ticking each colour; ask where the extra faces were hiding

misconceptions.belief: Mixes up edges and corners, for example says a cube has 8 edges
signs: Counts the pointy corners when asked for edges
Says 8 edges and 12 corners
Uses 'corner' and 'edge' as the same word

diagnostic.prompt_en: How many edges does a cube have?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek cube mein kitne edges hote hain?

remediation.representation: Stick-and-clay frame: sticks are edges, clay balls are corners
remediation.moveShape: Build the cube frame piece by piece; child names each new piece as edge or corner and keeps two separate tallies

misconceptions.belief: Thinks a cuboid has a different number of faces, edges or corners from a cube because its faces are different sizes
signs: Says a long biscuit box has more faces than a dice
Says a bigger box has more edges
Judges by how the solid looks instead of counting

diagnostic.prompt_en: A dice and a long biscuit box. Which one has more faces?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek dice aur ek lamba biscuit ka dabba. Kisme zyada faces hain?

options.text: The biscuit box, because it is bigger
The dice, because its faces are squares

remediation.representation: A dice and a matchbox side by side, faces ticked off together pair by pair
remediation.moveShape: Count both solids at the same time, top with top, front with front; ask what changed between them and what stayed the same

items.prompt_en: A dice is a cube. How many flat faces does it have?
items.prompt_hi: Dice ek cube hota hai. Iske kitne flat faces hain?
hints: What numbers are written on a dice?
Each number from 1 to 6 sits on its own face.
Numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, so faces = ___.
A dice has 6 faces, one for each number from 1 to 6.

items.prompt_en: Run your finger along a box where two faces meet. Is that line a face, an edge or a corner?
items.prompt_hi: Dabbe pe ungli wahan chalao jahan do faces milte hain. Woh line face hai, edge hai, ya corner?
items.answer: An edge
hints: What do you feel under your finger: something flat, a line, or a point?
Faces are flat and corners are points; the line between two faces has its own name.
The line where two faces meet is called an ___.
It is an edge: an edge is where two faces meet.

items.prompt_en: How many corners does a cube have?
items.prompt_hi: Ek cube ke kitne corners hote hain?
hints: How many corners does the top face have?
Count the corners of the top face, then the bottom face.
4 on top and 4 at the bottom make ___.
A cube has 8 corners: 4 on top and 4 at the bottom.

items.prompt_en: A carrom-striker box is a cuboid. In its picture you can see only 3 faces. Before we turn it around, guess: how many faces does the box really have?
items.prompt_hi: Carrom striker ka dabba ek cuboid hai. Picture mein sirf 3 faces dikhte hain. Ghumane se pehle guess karo: dabbe ke asal mein kitne faces hain?
hints: Can you see the bottom of the box in the picture?
There are faces at the back, at the bottom and on the far side too.
3 we can see + 3 hidden = ___.
6 faces: 3 we can see and 3 hidden behind, below and on the far side.

items.prompt_en: You said a cube has 6 faces, even though a picture shows only 3. How can you be sure?
items.prompt_hi: Tumne kaha cube ke 6 faces hain, jabki picture mein sirf 3 dikhte hain. Tumhe pakka kaise pata?
items.answer: Faces come in opposite pairs (top-bottom, front-back, left-right); every face we see has a hidden partner, so 3 seen + 3 hidden = 6
acceptable: top bottom front back left right
hints: Which face is opposite the top face?
Every face we can see has a face hiding on the other side.
Top and ___, front and ___, left and ___.
3 pairs of opposite faces make 6; the hidden 3 are behind, below and on the far side.

items.prompt_en: A dice is a cube and a matchbox is a cuboid. Which one has more edges?
items.prompt_hi: Dice ek cube hai aur maachis ki dibbi ek cuboid. Kisme zyada edges hain?
items.answer: Neither: both have 12 edges
hints: Do both have a top, a bottom and 4 sides?
Count the edges around the top, around the bottom, and the standing ones.
4 around the top + 4 around the bottom + 4 standing = ___.
Both have 12 edges; the matchbox's faces are longer but the count is the same.

items.prompt_en: Your tiffin box is a cuboid. How many edges and how many corners does it have?
items.prompt_hi: Tumhara tiffin box ek cuboid hai. Iske kitne edges aur kitne corners hain?
items.answer: 12 edges and 8 corners
hints: Is a tiffin box more like a matchbox or like a ball?
A cuboid is counted just like a cube.
12 edges and 8 corners, the same as any cube or cuboid.

items.prompt_en: I counted the edges of a cube and got 8. Did I count right?
items.prompt_hi: Maine cube ke edges gine aur 8 aaye. Kya maine sahi gina?
items.answer: No. 8 is the number of corners; a cube has 12 edges
hints: Which part of a cube is there 8 of?
Corners are points; edges are the lines between faces.
4 edges on top, 4 at the bottom, and ___ standing up.
No: I counted the corners. A cube has 12 edges and 8 corners.

items.prompt_en: Let us make a cube frame with sticks for the edges and clay balls for the corners. How many sticks and how many clay balls do we need?
items.prompt_hi: Chalo sticks aur clay ki goliyon se cube ka dhaancha banate hain. Sticks edges hain aur goliyan corners. Kitni sticks aur kitni goliyan chahiye?
items.answer: 12 sticks and 8 clay balls
hints: What does each stick stand for?
Sticks are edges and clay balls are corners.
Edges of a cube = ___, corners of a cube = ___.
12 sticks for the 12 edges and 8 clay balls for the 8 corners.

items.prompt_en: A paper pyramid has a square at the bottom and triangles on its sides that meet at the top. How many faces does it have?
items.prompt_hi: Ek kaagaz ka pyramid hai: neeche square, aur side mein triangles jo upar ek point pe milte hain. Iske kitne faces hain?
items.answer: 5 faces: 1 square and 4 triangles
hints: How many sides does the square at the bottom have?
One triangle stands on each side of the square.
1 square + ___ triangles = ___ faces.
5 faces: the square base and 4 triangles.

items.prompt_en: How many corners does that square pyramid have?
items.prompt_hi: Us square pyramid ke kitne corners hain?
items.answer: 5 corners
hints: How many corners does the square base have?
Count the base corners, then look at the very top.
4 at the bottom + ___ at the top = ___.
5 corners: 4 around the square and 1 at the tip.

items.prompt_en: Chintu says a cube has 3 faces because he can see only 3 in the picture. Explain to Chintu how to count all the faces.
items.prompt_hi: Chintu kehta hai cube ke 3 faces hain kyunki picture mein 3 hi dikhte hain. Chintu ko samjhao saare faces kaise ginte hain.
items.answer: Some faces hide at the back, bottom and far side; count in pairs (top-bottom, front-back, left-right) or turn the solid and tick each face: 6 faces
hints: What would you tell Chintu first?
Talk about the faces he cannot see in the picture.
Top and bottom, front and back, left and right: that is ___ faces.
Some faces are hidden; counting 3 pairs gives 6 faces.

items.prompt_en: Quick! A cube has how many faces, edges and corners?
items.prompt_hi: Jaldi batao! Cube ke kitne faces, edges aur corners hote hain?
items.answer: 6 faces, 12 edges, 8 corners
hints: Start with the faces: think of a dice.
Faces are flat, edges are lines, corners are points.
6 faces, ___ edges, ___ corners.
6 faces, 12 edges and 8 corners.

workedExample.problem: Count the faces, edges and corners of a matchbox.
steps: A matchbox is a cuboid.
Faces: top and bottom, front and back, left and right, so 6 faces.
Edges: 4 around the top, 4 around the bottom, 4 standing up, so 12 edges.
Corners: 4 on top and 4 at the bottom, so 8 corners.
fadedVersion: A matchbox is a ___.
Faces: top and bottom, front and back, left and right, so ___ faces.
Edges: 4 around the top, 4 around the bottom, ___ standing up, so ___ edges.
Corners: 4 on top and ___ at the bottom, so ___ corners.

skills.title: Recognise a right angle as a square corner and test for it with a folded-paper tester
Compare angles as less than, equal to or more than a right angle, whatever the length of the arms
Draw a circle with a string or bangle and know every point is the same distance from the centre

expectations: A right angle is a square corner, like the corner of a book; a paper folded twice makes a tester
An angle is about how wide the two arms open, not how long the arms are drawn
Turning a shape does not change its angles; a tilted square corner is still a right angle
In a circle every point on the edge is the same distance from the centre, which is why a tight string draws one

misconceptions.belief: Thinks an angle is bigger if its arms are drawn longer
signs: Picks the angle with longer lines as bigger
Says a big book's corner is a bigger angle than a small book's
Looks at the space covered rather than the opening

diagnostic.prompt_en: Two square corners are drawn: one with short lines and one with very long lines. Which angle is bigger?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Do square corner bane hain: ek chhoti lines se aur ek bahut lambi lines se. Kaunsa angle bada hai?

remediation.representation: Two-arm angle maker whose arms can be stretched without changing the opening
remediation.moveShape: Child fixes the opening, then stretches the arms longer and longer; ask whether the opening changed; then compare with a paper right-angle tester

misconceptions.belief: Thinks a right angle must have one arm flat and one arm standing; a tilted square corner is not a right angle
signs: Says a tile turned like a diamond has no right angles
Only finds right angles on things lying straight
Turns the page to 'fix' the angle before answering

diagnostic.prompt_en: A square tile is turned so it looks like a diamond. Are its corners still right angles?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek square tile ko ghuma diya, ab woh diamond jaisi dikhti hai. Kya uske corners ab bhi right angle hain?

options.text: Yes, turning does not change the corners
Only the top and bottom corners are

remediation.representation: A right-angle tester placed on a turning tile
remediation.moveShape: Child tests a corner, then the tile is rotated a little at a time and tested again; ask what turning changed and what it did not

misconceptions.belief: Thinks any round shape, like an egg or an oval, is a circle
signs: Calls an egg shape a circle
Draws a wobbly loop and calls it a circle
Does not mention a centre or equal distance

diagnostic.prompt_en: Which of these is a circle?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Inmein se circle kaunsa hai?

options.text: An egg shape, because it is round
Any round shape is a circle

remediation.representation: String compass: a pin, a string and a pencil, next to a hand-drawn oval
remediation.moveShape: Child measures from the centre to several points on both shapes; ask which one has all distances the same

items.prompt_en: Fold a paper twice to make a right-angle tester. Put it on a corner of your maths book. Does it fit exactly?
items.prompt_hi: Ek kaagaz ko do baar fold karke right-angle tester banao. Use apni maths book ke corner pe rakho. Kya woh bilkul fit hota hai?
items.answer: Yes, the book's corner is a right angle
hints: What kind of corner does a book have?
A paper folded twice makes a perfect square corner.
If the tester fits exactly, the corner is a ___ angle.
Yes, it fits exactly, so the book's corner is a right angle.

items.prompt_en: At 3 o'clock, do the two hands of a clock make a right angle?
items.prompt_hi: 3 baje ghadi ki dono suiyan kya right angle banati hain?
items.answer: Yes
hints: Where do the hands point at 3 o'clock?
One hand points straight up to 12 and one points across to 3.
Up and across like the corner of a ___.
Yes: one hand points up to 12 and one points across to 3, making a square corner.

items.prompt_en: I draw two square corners. One has arms 2 cm long and the other has arms 10 cm long. Guess: which angle is bigger?
items.prompt_hi: Main do square corner banata hoon. Ek ki lines 2 cm lambi hain aur doosre ki 10 cm. Guess karo: kaunsa angle bada hai?
items.answer: Neither: both are right angles, so they are the same
hints: What does the corner look like in both?
Longer arms do not open the corner any wider.
Both corners are ___ angles.
They are the same: both are right angles; only the arms are longer.

items.prompt_en: Why does drawing the arms of an angle longer not make the angle bigger?
items.prompt_hi: Angle ki lines ko lamba kar dene se angle bada kyun nahi hota?
items.answer: An angle is how wide the arms open (the amount of turn), not how long the arms are
hints: What changes when you open a pair of scissors wider?
Think of the opening between the arms, not their length.
An angle measures how wide the arms ___.
The angle is the opening between the arms; making the arms longer does not open it more.

items.prompt_en: Angle A opens just a little, like scissors opened slightly, but its arms are very long. Angle B is a square corner with short arms. Which angle is bigger?
items.prompt_hi: Angle A thoda sa khula hai, jaise kainchi thodi si khuli ho, par uski lines bahut lambi hain. Angle B ek square corner hai, chhoti lines ke saath. Kaunsa angle bada hai?
items.answer: Angle B
hints: Which one is opened wider?
Look at the opening, not the length of the lines.
A square corner opens wider than a slightly open pair of ___.
Angle B is bigger: it opens wider, even though its arms are shorter.

items.prompt_en: Which time has the clock hands making a right angle: 6 o'clock or 9 o'clock?
items.prompt_hi: Kis time pe ghadi ki suiyan right angle banati hain: 6 baje ya 9 baje?
items.answer: 9 o'clock
hints: Where do the hands point at 6 o'clock?
At 6 the hands make one straight line; at 9 one points up and one points across.
Up to 12 and across to 9 makes a ___ corner.
9 o'clock: one hand up to 12 and one across to 9 make a square corner; at 6 they make a straight line.

items.prompt_en: I turned a book so it is tilted like a diamond. I say its corners are not right angles any more. Am I right?
items.prompt_hi: Maine book ko tircha ghuma diya, ab woh diamond jaisi lagti hai. Main kehta hoon ab uske corners right angle nahi rahe. Kya main sahi hoon?
items.answer: No. Turning the book does not change its corners; they are still right angles
hints: Did the book itself change when we turned it?
Test a corner with your folded paper, in any direction.
Turning changes where the corner points, not the ___.
No: the corners are still right angles; turning only changes which way they face.

items.prompt_en: To draw a circle with a string and pencil, you hold one end of the string still with your finger. What is that still point called?
items.prompt_hi: String aur pencil se circle banane ke liye tum string ka ek sira ungli se dabake rakhte ho. Us point ko kya kehte hain?
items.answer: The centre
hints: Where is that point compared to the circle?
It is in the very middle of the circle.
The middle point of a circle is its ___.
It is the centre of the circle.

items.prompt_en: You tie a pencil to a 5 cm string and turn it around a pin, keeping the string tight. How far from the pin is every point on the circle?
items.prompt_hi: Tumne pencil ko 5 cm ki string se baandha aur string tight rakhkar pin ke chaaron taraf ghumaya. Circle ka har point pin se kitni door hai?
items.answer: 5 cm
hints: How long is the string?
The tight string is the distance from the pin to the pencil.
Every point is ___ cm from the pin.
5 cm: the tight string keeps every point 5 cm from the centre.

items.prompt_en: An egg shape and the shape of a bangle. Which one is a circle, and how can you check?
items.prompt_hi: Ek ande ka shape aur ek chudi ka shape. Inmein circle kaunsa hai, aur kaise check karoge?
items.answer: The bangle; every point on it is the same distance from the centre
hints: Is the egg the same width all the way round?
Measure from the middle to the edge in different directions.
In a circle every point is the ___ distance from the centre.
The bangle is a circle: from its centre every point on it is equally far; the egg is longer one way.

items.prompt_en: To draw a big circle in the playground, Ravi ties a 2 m rope to a peg and walks around with chalk tied at the other end. Why must he keep the rope tight?
items.prompt_hi: Playground mein bada circle banane ke liye Ravi 2 m ki rassi ek khoonte se baandhta hai aur doosre sire pe chalk lagakar chaaron taraf chalta hai. Rassi tight kyun rakhni padegi?
items.answer: So that every point he draws is exactly 2 m from the peg; a loose rope gives a wobbly shape that is not a circle
hints: What happens to the chalk if the rope goes loose?
The rope's job is to keep the chalk the same distance from the peg.
A tight rope keeps every point ___ m from the centre.
A tight rope keeps every chalk mark 2 m from the peg; loose, the distance changes and it is not a circle.

items.prompt_en: Teach Golu how to check whether a corner is a right angle using a folded paper. Also tell him whether longer arms make an angle bigger.
items.prompt_hi: Golu ko sikhao folded paper se kaise check karte hain ki corner right angle hai ya nahi. Aur use yeh bhi batao ki lambi lines se angle bada hota hai ya nahi.
items.answer: Fold paper twice to get a square corner, put it on the corner: if it fits exactly it is a right angle, if the corner is narrower it is less, if wider it is more; longer arms do not change the angle
hints: What would you tell Golu to do first with the paper?
Talk about folding, fitting, and what the size of an angle means.
Fold twice, place it on the corner; if it fits ___ it is a right angle.
Fold the paper twice, place the square corner on the angle and see if it fits exactly; the length of the arms does not change an angle.

items.prompt_en: Quick! Name two things in your room that have right-angle corners.
items.prompt_hi: Jaldi batao! Apne kamre mein do cheezein batao jinke corners right angle hain.
items.answer: Any two square-corner things, such as a book, a door, a window, a table top or a notebook
hints: Look at the corners of things around you.
Think of things that are rectangles.
A book, a door, a ___.
For example a book and a door: their corners are square corners.

workedExample.problem: Is the corner of a window a right angle? Check it.
steps: Take a paper and fold it in half, then fold it in half again to make a square corner.
Place the folded corner into the window's corner.
The paper fits exactly with no gap and no overlap.
So the window's corner is a right angle.
fadedVersion: Take a paper and fold it in half, then fold it in half ___ to make a square corner.
Place the folded corner into the window's ___.
The paper fits ___ with no gap and no overlap.
So the window's corner is a ___ angle.

skills.title: Copy a shape on a dot or square grid by counting units along each side
Recognise that a shape turned or moved on a grid is still the same shape and size
Make and continue tile patterns on a grid

expectations: To copy a shape exactly, count the units (gaps between dots or sides of squares) along every side
A line touching 5 dots in a row is 4 units long: count the gaps, not the dots
Turning or sliding a shape does not change its side lengths, its corners or how many squares it covers
A slanting line across a square is longer than one side of that square

misconceptions.belief: Thinks a shape on a grid becomes a different shape when it is turned
signs: Calls a turned square a 'diamond, not a square'
Says a standing strip and a lying strip are different shapes
Recounts the squares after a turn expecting a new number

diagnostic.prompt_en: A square on the grid is turned so it stands on one corner. What is it now?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Grid pe ek square ko ghuma diya, ab woh ek corner pe khada hai. Ab woh kya hai?

options.text: A diamond, not a square any more

remediation.representation: Cut-out shape on a transparent overlay that the child can turn over the grid
remediation.moveShape: Child traces the shape, turns the tracing and lays it back on the original; ask what stayed the same

misconceptions.belief: Counts dots instead of the gaps between them when measuring a line on a dot grid
signs: Says a line touching 4 dots is 4 units long
Copied shapes come out one unit too long
Points at dots while counting instead of at spaces

diagnostic.prompt_en: A line on a dot grid touches 6 dots in a row. How many units long is it?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Dot grid pe ek line ek row mein 6 dots ko chhooti hai. Woh line kitni units lambi hai?

remediation.representation: Number line under the dot row, with each jump between dots highlighted
remediation.moveShape: Child hops a finger from dot to dot, counting hops not dots; compare the hop count with the dot count

misconceptions.belief: Thinks a slanting line from corner to corner of a grid square is the same length as one side
signs: Counts each slanting step as 1 unit
Says a slanted shape and a straight shape have the same side lengths
Copies a slanted side with a straight one

diagnostic.prompt_en: Which is longer: one side of a grid square, or the slanting line from corner to corner of the same square?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Kaun lamba hai: grid ke ek square ki ek side, ya usi square ke ek corner se doosre corner tak ki tirchi line?

remediation.representation: Strip of paper marked with one unit, laid along a side and then along the slanting line
remediation.moveShape: Child measures both with the same paper strip and notices the slanting line sticks out past one unit

items.prompt_en: On a square grid, a rectangle is 4 squares long and 2 squares tall. How many small squares are inside it?
items.prompt_hi: Square grid pe ek rectangle 4 squares lamba aur 2 squares ooncha hai. Uske andar kitne chhote squares hain?
hints: How many squares are in the bottom row?
There are 2 rows with 4 squares in each.
8 squares: 2 rows of 4.

items.prompt_en: On a dot grid, you draw a line from one dot to the 5th dot in the same row. How many units long is the line?
items.prompt_hi: Dot grid pe tum ek dot se usi row ke 5th dot tak line banate ho. Line kitni units lambi hai?
items.answer: 4 units
hints: Are we counting dots or the gaps between them?
A unit is one gap between two dots next to each other.
5 dots have ___ gaps between them.
4 units: 5 dots in a row have 4 gaps.

items.prompt_en: I make an L shape on the grid using 4 squares. Now I turn the paper around. Guess: how many squares will the L have now?
items.prompt_hi: Main grid pe 4 squares se ek L shape banata hoon. Ab paper ghuma deta hoon. Guess karo: ab L mein kitne squares honge?
items.answer: Still 4
hints: Did we add or remove any squares?
Turning the paper moves the shape but does not change it.
Before turning: 4 squares. After turning: ___ squares.
Still 4 squares: turning does not change the shape.

items.prompt_en: Why is a square turned to look like a diamond still a square?
items.prompt_hi: Ghumaya hua square, jo diamond jaisa dikhta hai, ab bhi square kyun hai?
items.answer: Its 4 sides are still equal and its corners are still right angles; turning does not change sides or angles
hints: What makes a shape a square?
Check its sides and its corners after turning.
All 4 sides are still ___ and all corners are still ___ angles.
It is still a square: 4 equal sides and 4 right angles, just facing a new way.

items.prompt_en: Shape A is a strip of 3 squares lying flat. Shape B is a strip of 3 squares standing up. Are they the same shape and size, or different?
items.prompt_hi: Shape A 3 squares ki ek patti hai jo leti hui hai. Shape B 3 squares ki patti hai jo khadi hai. Kya dono same shape aur size ke hain, ya alag?
items.answer: The same shape and size; B is A turned
hints: How many squares does each strip have?
Imagine turning strip A until it stands up.
Both are 3 squares in a line; one is just ___.
They are the same: strip B is strip A turned to stand up.

items.prompt_en: Copy a T shape: 3 squares across the top and 2 squares going down from the middle square. How many squares are there in all?
items.prompt_hi: Ek T shape copy karo: upar 3 squares aur beech wale square se neeche 2 squares. Total kitne squares hain?
hints: How many squares are in the top row?
Add the top row and the squares going down.
5 squares: 3 across the top and 2 going down.

items.prompt_en: Riya wanted a line 3 units long on a dot grid, so she joined 3 dots. Is her line 3 units long?
items.prompt_hi: Riya ko dot grid pe 3 unit lambi line chahiye thi, isliye usne 3 dots joda. Kya uski line 3 unit lambi hai?
items.answer: No. Joining 3 dots makes a line 2 units long; she needs 4 dots
hints: How many gaps are between 3 dots?
Count the hops from dot to dot.
3 dots make ___ gaps; for 3 units we need ___ dots.
No: 3 dots make 2 units; a 3-unit line touches 4 dots.

items.prompt_en: A tile pattern on a grid goes red, blue, blue, red, blue, blue, and so on. Say it with letters R and B. What colour is the 7th tile?
items.prompt_hi: Grid pe tiles ka pattern hai: red, blue, blue, red, blue, blue, aur aise hi aage. Ise R aur B letters se bolo. 7th tile kis colour ki hogi?
items.answer: Red
hints: Which part keeps repeating?
R B B is one block; it repeats again and again.
R B B, R B B, then the 7th is ___.
Red: R B B R B B R, so the 7th tile is red.

items.prompt_en: A courtyard floor is 5 tiles long and 4 tiles wide. All the tiles along the border are red and the ones inside are white. How many white tiles are there?
items.prompt_hi: Ek aangan ka farsh 5 tiles lamba aur 4 tiles chauda hai. Kinare ki saari tiles red hain aur andar wali white. Kitni white tiles hain?
hints: If you take away the border, how long is the inside part?
Remove one tile from each end of the length and of the width.
Inside is 3 long and 2 wide, so 3 + 3 = ___.
6 white tiles: the inside part is 3 tiles by 2 tiles.

items.prompt_en: On a square grid, line A goes along one side of a small square. Line B goes slanting from one corner to the opposite corner of the same square. Are they the same length?
items.prompt_hi: Square grid pe line A ek chhote square ki ek side ke saath jaati hai. Line B usi square ke ek corner se saamne wale corner tak tirchi jaati hai. Kya dono ki lambai barabar hai?
items.answer: No, the slanting line B is longer
hints: Which line goes further across the square?
Measure both with the same paper strip.
The slanting line sticks out past ___ unit.
No: the slanting line B is longer than one side.

items.prompt_en: Teach Golu how to copy a shape exactly on a dot grid.
items.prompt_hi: Golu ko sikhao dot grid pe shape bilkul same kaise copy karte hain.
items.answer: Start at a dot, count the gaps (units) along each side of the shape and draw the same number of gaps in the same direction; check the corners match
hints: What would you tell Golu to count?
Talk about counting gaps, not dots, side by side.
For each side: count the ___ and go the same way.
Count the units along each side and draw the same number in the same direction, side after side.

48: each number is double the one before, so after 24 comes 48.

Every step adds ___, so 11 + 3 = 14.

items.prompt_en: 100, 90, 80, ___, ___. What are the next two numbers?
items.prompt_hi: 100, 90, 80, ___, ___. Agle do number kya hain?
items.answer: 70 and 60

items.answer: No. The next Monday is the 12th, because a week has 7 days

items.prompt_en: Matchstick triangles in a row: 1 triangle needs 3 sticks, 2 joined triangles need 5, 3 joined triangles need 7. Say the rule. How many sticks for 4 triangles?

hints: How many more sticks for each new triangle?

9 sticks: each new triangle adds 2 sticks.

items.prompt_en: Pinki saves ₹5 on day 1, ₹10 on day 2, ₹15 on day 3, and each day she saves ₹5 more than the day before. How much will she save on day 6?

hints: What does she save on day 4?
Keep adding ₹5 for each new day.

items.prompt_en: On a calendar, the dates in one column go 3, 10, 17, ___. What comes next?
items.prompt_hi: Calendar ke ek column mein tareekhein hain 3, 10, 17, ___. Aage kya aayega?

Each date in a column is one week after the one above.
24: each step down a column adds 7.

items.prompt_en: Teach Golu how to find the next number in any number pattern.

Find the ___ between numbers, check ___ step, then use the rule.

items.prompt_hi: Jaldi batao! 64, 60, 56, ___?

The next number is ___.

skills.title: Read and write 4-digit numbers in words and in numerals

Write 4-digit numbers that have zeros inside them, and their expanded form

misconceptions.belief: Writes numbers the way they are spoken, joining the parts, for example four thousand fifty as 400050 or 40050
signs: Writes 'five thousand twenty' as 500020
Writes more than 4 digits for a number under ten thousand

diagnostic.prompt_en: Write 'four thousand fifty' in numbers.

4709 notebooks.

items.prompt_en: On a number line from 0 to 10000, guess before marking: will 1000 be close to 0, or near the middle?

items.prompt_en: Which is bigger: 999 or 1000?

1000: it is one more than 999.

items.prompt_en: Teach Golu how to decide which of two 4-digit numbers is bigger.

items.prompt_en: Quick! What is the smallest 4-digit number?
