items.prompt_hi: Number line pe check karne se pehle guess karo: 1450, 1000 ke paas hai ya 2000 ke?
items.answer: Nearer 1000
hints: What is halfway between 1000 and 2000?
Halfway is 1500; 1450 has not reached it.
1450 is below ___, so it is nearer ___.
Nearer 1000: 1450 is below the halfway mark 1500.

items.prompt_en: You rounded 2380 to 2000 for the nearest thousand. Why not 3000?
items.prompt_hi: Tumne 2380 ko nearest thousand mein 2000 kiya. 3000 kyun nahi?
items.answer: 2380 is between 2000 and 3000 and the halfway mark is 2500; 2380 is below halfway, so it is nearer 2000
hints: What is halfway between 2000 and 3000?
Compare 2380 with the halfway mark.
2380 is ___ 2500, so it goes to ___.
2380 is below the halfway mark 2500, so it is nearer 2000.

items.prompt_en: Round 1249 and 1251 to the nearest 100.
items.prompt_hi: 1249 aur 1251 dono ko nearest 100 mein round karo.
hints: Which digit decides for the nearest hundred?
Look at the tens digit, compared to the halfway mark 1250.
1249 is below 1250 so ___; 1251 is above so ___.
1249 rounds to 1200 and 1251 rounds to 1300: one is just below halfway, one just above.

items.prompt_en: About 4870 people live in a village. Round that to the nearest 1000.
items.prompt_hi: Ek gaon mein lagbhag 4870 log rehte hain. Ise nearest 1000 mein round karo.
hints: Which two thousands is 4870 between?
4000 and 5000; halfway is 4500.

items.prompt_en: I rounded 3460 to the nearest thousand like this: 3460 → 3500 → 4000. Is that right?
items.prompt_hi: Maine 3460 ko nearest thousand mein aise round kiya: 3460 → 3500 → 4000. Kya yeh sahi hai?
items.answer: No. 3460 is below the halfway mark 3500, so it rounds to 3000
hints: Is 3460 itself above or below 3500?
Round once, from the number you started with.
3460 is ___ 3500, so it rounds to ___.
No: 3460 is below 3500, so the nearest thousand is 3000; rounding twice moved it up wrongly.

items.prompt_en: On a number line from 5000 to 6000 with a mark at 5500, where does 5720 sit? Which thousand is it nearer?
items.prompt_hi: 5000 se 6000 ki number line pe 5500 pe ek mark hai. 5720 kahan aayega? Woh kis thousand ke paas hai?
items.answer: Past the 5500 mark, so nearer 6000
hints: Is 5720 more or less than 5500?
Past the halfway mark means it is nearer the upper thousand.
Past the 5500 mark, so 5720 is nearer 6000.

items.prompt_en: A train has 1186 passengers. The newspaper says 'about 1200 passengers'. To which place did they round: nearest 10, 100 or 1000?
items.prompt_hi: Ek train mein 1186 yaatri hain. Akhbaar likhta hai 'lagbhag 1200 yaatri'. Unhone kis place tak round kiya: nearest 10, 100 ya 1000?
items.answer: To the nearest 100
hints: What would 1186 be to the nearest 10?
Nearest 10 gives 1190; nearest 1000 gives 1000.
1186 to the nearest ___ is 1200.
The nearest 100: 1186 is between 1100 and 1200, and nearer 1200.

items.prompt_en: Ravi rounded 2890 to the nearest thousand and got 2000, because he just dropped the last digits. Is he right?
items.prompt_hi: Ravi ne 2890 ko nearest thousand mein round kiya aur 2000 bola, kyunki usne bas aakhri digits hata diye. Kya woh sahi hai?
items.answer: No. 2890 is past 2500, so it rounds to 3000
hints: Is 2890 nearer 2000 or 3000?
Rounding means choosing the nearer neighbour, not cutting off digits.
No: 2890 is much nearer 3000, so it rounds to 3000.

items.prompt_en: Teach Golu how to round 3650 to the nearest 1000.
items.prompt_hi: Golu ko sikhao 3650 ko nearest 1000 mein kaise round karte hain.
items.answer: Find the neighbours 3000 and 4000, find the halfway mark 3500; 3650 is past halfway, so it rounds to 4000
hints: What should Golu find first?
Talk about the two neighbours and the halfway mark.
Neighbours 3000 and ___; halfway ___; 3650 is past it so ___.
Neighbours 3000 and 4000, halfway 3500; 3650 is past halfway, so 4000.

items.prompt_en: Quick! 8500 rounded to the nearest thousand?
items.prompt_hi: Jaldi batao! 8500 ko nearest thousand mein round karo?
hints: Is 8500 exactly halfway?
Halfway rounds up.
8500 goes up to ___.
9000: halfway rounds up.

workedExample.problem: Round 7380 to the nearest thousand.
steps: 7380 is between 7000 and 8000.
The halfway mark is 7500.
7380 is less than 7500.
So 7380 rounds to 7000.
fadedVersion: 7380 is between 7000 and ___.
The halfway mark is ___.
So 7380 rounds to ___.

skills.title: Recognise equal parts and name halves, thirds and quarters of a shape
Find a fraction of a collection, such as 1/2 of 8 or 1/3 of 12
Compare unit fractions like 1/2, 1/3 and 1/4 of the same whole

expectations: A fraction names equal parts of one whole; the parts must be the same size
The bottom number says how many equal parts the whole is cut into; the top says how many we take
The more equal parts a whole is cut into, the smaller each part is, so 1/4 is less than 1/2
A fraction of a collection is found by sharing the collection into equal groups

misconceptions.belief: Believes 1/3 is bigger than 1/2 because 3 is bigger than 2 (whole-number bias)
signs: Picks 1/4 of a roti over 1/2 as 'more'
Orders unit fractions by the bottom number
Says 1/10 is the biggest

diagnostic.prompt_en: Which is bigger: 1/3 of a roti or 1/2 of the same roti?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Kaun bada hai: ek roti ka 1/3 ya usi roti ka 1/2?

remediation.representation: Fraction bars of the same length cut into 2, 3 and 4 equal pieces, laid one above the other
remediation.moveShape: Child predicts which piece is longest, then lays one piece from each bar side by side; ask what happens to each piece when we cut into more parts

misconceptions.belief: Thinks the parts need not be equal to be called halves, thirds or quarters
signs: Calls any 3 pieces 'thirds'
Cuts a cake into 4 uneven pieces and calls each a quarter
Counts pieces without checking size

diagnostic.prompt_en: A rope is cut into 3 pieces of different lengths. Is each piece one-third of the rope?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek rassi ke 3 tukde kiye gaye jo alag-alag lambai ke hain. Kya har tukda rassi ka ek-tihaai hai?

options.text: No, the pieces must be equal

remediation.representation: Fair-sharing story: three friends and one big piece of watermelon among small ones
remediation.moveShape: Child decides whether the sharing is fair; then fold a paper strip into 3 equal parts and compare with the uneven cut

misconceptions.belief: Names a fraction as parts taken compared with parts left (part to part), not parts out of the whole
signs: Calls 1 shaded out of 4 parts '1/3'
Uses the number of unshaded parts as the bottom number
Says 'one out of three left'

diagnostic.prompt_en: A chocolate bar has 5 equal parts and 2 are eaten. What fraction is eaten?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek chocolate mein 5 barabar tukde hain aur 2 kha liye. Kitna hissa khaya?

remediation.representation: Bar with every part numbered, the whole outlined in bold
remediation.moveShape: Child counts all the parts of the whole first and says that number aloud, then counts the eaten parts; ask which number tells the whole

items.prompt_en: A roti is cut into 4 equal pieces. What do we call one piece?
items.prompt_hi: Ek roti ke 4 barabar tukde kiye. Ek tukde ko kya kehte hain?
items.answer: One quarter, 1/4
hints: How many equal pieces is the whole roti cut into?
One piece out of 4 equal pieces.
1 out of 4 is written 1/___.
One quarter, 1/4: one of 4 equal pieces.

items.prompt_en: What is half of 10 laddoos?
items.prompt_hi: 10 laddoo ka aadha kitna hai?
hints: How many groups do we share into for a half?
Share 10 into 2 equal groups.
10 shared into 2 equal groups gives ___ each.
5: half of 10 is 5.

items.prompt_en: Share 12 bananas equally among 3 friends. What is 1/3 of 12?
items.prompt_hi: 12 kele 3 doston mein barabar baanto. 12 ka 1/3 kitna hai?
hints: How many equal groups make thirds?
Make 3 equal groups from 12.
3 groups of ___ make 12.
4: each friend gets 4, so 1/3 of 12 is 4.

items.prompt_en: One cake is shared by 2 children, and another cake of the same size is shared by 3 children. Guess: who gets a bigger piece, a child in the group of 2 or in the group of 3?
items.prompt_hi: Ek cake 2 bachchon mein baanta, aur utna hi bada doosra cake 3 bachchon mein. Guess karo: kiska tukda bada hoga, 2 wale group ke bachche ka ya 3 wale ka?
items.answer: A child in the group of 2 (1/2 is more than 1/3)
hints: When more people share the same cake, what happens to each piece?
More sharers means smaller pieces.
The child in the group of 2: half a cake is more than a third.

items.prompt_en: You said 1/2 is bigger than 1/4. Why, when 4 is bigger than 2?
items.prompt_hi: Tumne kaha 1/2, 1/4 se bada hai. Kyun, jabki 4, 2 se bada hai?
items.answer: The bottom number is how many equal parts the whole is cut into; more parts means each part is smaller
hints: What does the 4 in 1/4 tell us?
Think of one roti cut into 2 pieces and one cut into 4.
Cutting into more parts makes each part ___.
1/2 is bigger: cutting the same whole into 4 parts makes each part smaller than cutting it into 2.

items.prompt_en: Watermelon A is cut into 3 pieces: one big and two small. Watermelon B is cut into 3 pieces of the same size. In which one is each piece one-third?
items.prompt_hi: Tarbooz A ke 3 tukde kiye: ek bada aur do chhote. Tarbooz B ke 3 tukde kiye, sab barabar. Kisme har tukda ek-tihaai hai?
items.answer: Watermelon B
hints: Are A's pieces fair to everyone?
Thirds must be 3 equal parts.
Only the watermelon with ___ pieces has thirds.
B: its 3 pieces are equal, so each is one-third; A's pieces are not.

items.prompt_en: A chocolate has 4 equal pieces and I ate 1. I say I ate 1/3 because 3 pieces are left. Am I right?
items.prompt_hi: Ek chocolate mein 4 barabar tukde hain aur maine 1 khaaya. Main kehta hoon maine 1/3 khaaya kyunki 3 tukde bache. Kya main sahi hoon?
items.answer: No. I ate 1/4, one piece out of 4 equal pieces in the whole
hints: How many pieces were in the whole chocolate?
The bottom number counts all the parts of the whole, not the ones left.
1 out of ___ is 1/___.
No: it is 1/4, because the whole had 4 equal pieces.

items.prompt_en: What is 1/4 of 20 marbles?
items.prompt_hi: 20 kanchon ka 1/4 kitna hai?
hints: How many equal groups do we make for quarters?
Share 20 into 4 equal groups.
4 groups of ___ make 20.
5: 20 shared into 4 equal groups gives 5 in each.

items.prompt_en: Picture a square paper folded into 4 equal parts with 3 parts coloured. Say the coloured part as a fraction.
items.prompt_hi: Socho ek square kaagaz 4 barabar hisson mein fold hai aur 3 hisse rang diye. Rangin hissa fraction mein batao.
hints: How many equal parts in the whole?
3 coloured parts out of 4 equal parts.
Coloured = ___/4.
3/4: three of the four equal parts are coloured.

items.prompt_en: There are 24 students in a class. Half of them play cricket and a quarter of them play kho-kho. How many play each game?
items.prompt_hi: Ek class mein 24 bachche hain. Aadhe cricket khelte hain aur ek-chauthaai kho-kho. Kaun sa khel kitne bachche khelte hain?
items.answer: 12 play cricket and 6 play kho-kho
hints: What is half of 24?
Half means 2 equal groups; a quarter means 4 equal groups.
Half of 24 = ___; a quarter of 24 = ___.
12 play cricket and 6 play kho-kho.

items.prompt_en: Arrange from the biggest piece to the smallest: 1/3, 1/2 and 1/4 of the same roti.
items.prompt_hi: Ek hi roti ke 1/3, 1/2 aur 1/4 ko sabse bade tukde se sabse chhote tak lagao.
hints: Which cut makes the fewest pieces?
Fewer equal pieces means bigger pieces.
Biggest is 1/___, smallest is 1/___.
1/2, then 1/3, then 1/4.

items.prompt_en: Teach Golu what 'one-third' means. Use a roti in your explanation.
items.prompt_hi: Golu ko sikhao 'ek-tihaai' ka matlab kya hai. Roti ka example lo.
items.answer: One-third is one of 3 equal parts of a whole; cut the roti into 3 pieces of the same size, and one piece is 1/3; unequal pieces are not thirds
hints: How many pieces should Golu cut the roti into?
Talk about the pieces being the same size.
Cut into ___ equal pieces; one piece is ___.
Cut the roti into 3 equal pieces; one of them is one-third.

items.prompt_en: Quick! Which is more: 1/2 of a pizza or 1/4 of the same pizza?
items.prompt_hi: Jaldi batao! Kya zyada hai: ek pizza ka 1/2 ya usi pizza ka 1/4?
hints: Which cut makes bigger pieces?
Half is 2 pieces; a quarter is 4 pieces.
Fewer pieces are ___.
1/2 of the pizza is more.

workedExample.problem: What is 1/3 of 15 pencils?
steps: 1/3 means 1 of 3 equal groups.
Share 15 pencils into 3 equal groups.
Each group gets 5 pencils, because 3 groups of 5 make 15.
So 1/3 of 15 is 5.
fadedVersion: 1/3 means 1 of ___ equal groups.
Share 15 pencils into ___ equal groups.
Each group gets ___ pencils, because 3 groups of 5 make 15.
So 1/3 of 15 is ___.

skills.title: Know half, quarter and three-quarter of a kilogram and of a litre in grams and millilitres
Know half, quarter and three-quarter of a metre in centimetres
Combine fractions of a measure, such as half kilo plus quarter kilo

expectations: 1 kg = 1000 g, so half a kilo is 500 g, a quarter kilo (paav) is 250 g and three-quarters is 750 g
1 litre = 1000 ml, so half a litre is 500 ml and a quarter litre is 250 ml
1 m = 100 cm, so half a metre is 50 cm and a quarter metre is 25 cm
A fraction of a measure depends on the size of the whole, not on the number of packets or pieces

misconceptions.belief: Thinks 3/4 means 3 pieces, whatever their size
signs: Says 3 small packets of 100 g is three-quarter kilo
Counts packets instead of weighing
Thinks any 3 glasses make three-quarter litre

diagnostic.prompt_en: Which is three-quarters of a kilo: 3 packets of 50 g, or 750 g?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Teen-chauthaai kilo kaunsa hai: 50-50 g ke 3 packet, ya 750 g?

options.text: 3 packets of 50 g, because it is 3 pieces

remediation.representation: Balance scale with a 1 kg weight on one side and quarter-kilo packets on the other
remediation.moveShape: Child adds quarter-kilo packets one by one and says the total each time; then tries 3 small packets and sees the scale does not match

misconceptions.belief: Thinks half of any measure is 50, for example half a kilo is 50 g
signs: Says half a litre is 50 ml
Uses 50 for half of every unit
Mixes up metres and kilograms

diagnostic.prompt_en: Half a litre of oil is how many ml?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Aadha litre tel kitne ml hai?

remediation.representation: Measuring jug marked 0 to 1000 ml with the halfway line highlighted
remediation.moveShape: Child pours to the halfway line and reads the mark; ask how many ml the full jug holds and what half of that is

misconceptions.belief: Links 'quarter' with the number 4, so says a quarter kilo is 400 g or 4 g
signs: Says paav kilo is 400 g
Says a quarter litre is 4 ml
Writes 1/4 kg as 0.4 kg

diagnostic.prompt_en: A quarter kilo is how many grams?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Paav kilo kitne gram hota hai?

remediation.representation: Four equal packets that together balance 1 kg
remediation.moveShape: Child shares 1000 g into 4 equal packets and names the weight of one; ask how many quarter packets make the kilo

items.prompt_en: Half a kilo of tomatoes is how many grams?
items.prompt_hi: Aadha kilo tamatar kitne gram hote hain?
hints: How many grams make a whole kilo?
1 kg is 1000 g; half means 2 equal parts.
Half of 1000 = ___.
500 g: half of 1000 g.

items.prompt_en: Paav kilo dhaniya, a quarter kilo of coriander, is how many grams?
items.prompt_hi: Paav kilo dhaniya, yaani ek-chauthaai kilo, kitne gram hai?
hints: How many grams in 1 kg?
A quarter means 1000 g shared into 4 equal parts.
4 groups of ___ make 1000.
250 g: 1000 g shared into 4 equal parts.

items.prompt_en: Half a metre of ribbon is how many centimetres?
items.prompt_hi: Aadha metre ribbon kitne centimetre hai?
items.answer: 50 cm
hints: How many cm in 1 m?
1 m is 100 cm; take half of it.
Half of 100 = ___.
50 cm: half of 100 cm.

items.prompt_en: Guess: a quarter-litre glass of lassi holds 250 ml or 400 ml?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: paav litre lassi ke glass mein 250 ml aata hai ya 400 ml?
items.answer: 250 ml
hints: How many ml in a litre?
A quarter is one of 4 equal parts of 1000 ml.
1000 shared by 4 = ___.
250 ml: four such glasses fill 1 litre.

items.prompt_en: Why is three-quarter kilo 750 g?
items.prompt_hi: Teen-chauthaai kilo 750 g kyun hota hai?
items.answer: A kilo is 1000 g; a quarter is 250 g; three quarters is 3 × 250 = 750 g
hints: What is one quarter of a kilo?
Three-quarters means three of those quarter parts.
One quarter is 250 g, so three quarters is 750 g.

items.prompt_en: Shopkeeper A gives you 3 small packets of sugar, 100 g each. Shopkeeper B gives you three-quarter kilo. Who gives more sugar?
items.prompt_hi: Dukaandaar A tumhe chini ke 3 chhote packet deta hai, har ek 100 g. Dukaandaar B teen-chauthaai kilo deta hai. Kaun zyada chini deta hai?
items.answer: B: 750 g is more than 300 g
hints: How much is 3 packets of 100 g?
Three-quarter kilo is 750 g, whatever the packets.
A gives ___ g and B gives ___ g.
B gives more: 750 g is more than 300 g.

items.prompt_en: Three-quarter litre of milk is how many ml?
items.prompt_hi: Teen-chauthaai litre doodh kitne ml hai?
items.answer: 750 ml
hints: What is a quarter litre?
A quarter litre is 250 ml; take three of them.

items.prompt_en: I said half a kilo of onions is 50 g. Am I right?
items.prompt_hi: Maine kaha aadha kilo pyaaz 50 g hai. Kya main sahi hoon?
items.answer: No. Half a kilo is 500 g
hints: How many grams make a whole kilo?
Half of 1000, not half of 100.
Half of 1000 = ___.
No: half a kilo is 500 g.

items.prompt_en: A jug has marks for 1/4 l, 1/2 l, 3/4 l and 1 l. Say each mark in ml.
items.prompt_hi: Ek jug pe 1/4 l, 1/2 l, 3/4 l aur 1 l ke nishaan hain. Har nishaan ml mein batao.
hints: What is the full litre in ml?
Each quarter step adds 250 ml.
250 ml, 500 ml, 750 ml and 1000 ml.

items.prompt_en: Amma buys half a kilo of potatoes and a quarter kilo of peas. How many grams is that altogether? Is it more or less than 1 kg?
items.prompt_hi: Amma aadha kilo aaloo aur paav kilo matar khareedti hain. Kul kitne gram hue? Yeh 1 kg se zyada hai ya kam?
items.answer: 750 g, less than 1 kg
hints: What is half a kilo in grams? A quarter?
500 g and 250 g; add them.
750 g altogether, which is less than 1 kg.

items.prompt_en: Three-quarter metre of cloth is how many cm?
items.prompt_hi: Teen-chauthaai metre kapda kitne cm hai?
items.answer: 75 cm
hints: What is a quarter of 100 cm?
A quarter metre is 25 cm; take three of them.
75 cm.

items.prompt_en: Teach Golu how to find how many grams are in a quarter kilo.
items.prompt_hi: Golu ko sikhao paav kilo mein kitne gram hote hain, kaise nikaalte hain.
items.answer: 1 kg is 1000 g; a quarter means 4 equal parts; 1000 shared into 4 equal parts is 250 g
hints: What should Golu start with?
Talk about the whole kilo and the 4 equal parts.
1000 g into ___ equal parts is ___ g each.
Start from 1000 g, share it into 4 equal parts, and each part is 250 g.

items.prompt_en: Quick! How many 250 g packets make 1 kg?
items.prompt_hi: Jaldi batao! 250 g ke kitne packet milkar 1 kg bante hain?
hints: Count up in 250s to 1000.
That is ___ packets.
4 packets.

workedExample.problem: How many grams is three-quarter kilo of rice?
steps: A quarter kilo is 1000 g shared into 4 equal parts, which is 250 g.
Three-quarters is 3 of those parts: 250 + 250 + 250.
So three-quarter kilo is 750 g.
fadedVersion: A quarter kilo is 1000 g shared into ___ equal parts, which is 250 g.
Three-quarters is ___ of those parts: 250 + 250 + 250.
So three-quarter kilo is ___ g.

skills.title: Measure a length with a ruler by starting at the 0 mark
Convert between metres and centimetres using 1 m = 100 cm
Estimate lengths and choose cm or m as the unit

expectations: Length is the number of 1 cm spaces from one end to the other, so start at 0, not at the edge or at 1
If you start at another mark, take the start reading away from the end reading
1 metre is 100 centimetres; 1 m 5 cm is 105 cm, not 15 cm
Use centimetres for small things and metres for big things like rooms and pitches

misconceptions.belief: Believes 1 m = 10 cm
signs: Says 2 m is 20 cm
Says 90 cm is longer than 1 m
Mixes metres with tens

diagnostic.prompt_en: How many cm is 1 m?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: 1 m mein kitne cm hote hain?

remediation.representation: A real metre tape laid next to 10 one-cm cubes
remediation.moveShape: Child lays 10 cm against the metre tape and sees how short it is; count how many tens fit along the metre

misconceptions.belief: Starts measuring from the edge of the ruler or from 1 instead of 0, or reads only the end number
signs: Says an object from 3 to 9 is 9 cm long
Lines up the object with the ruler's edge
Gets answers 1 cm too long

diagnostic.prompt_en: A leaf lies from the 1 mark to the 7 mark on a ruler. How long is it?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek patta ruler pe 1 ke nishaan se 7 ke nishaan tak hai. Woh kitna lamba hai?

remediation.representation: Broken ruler that starts at 4, with each 1 cm space highlighted
remediation.moveShape: Child counts the spaces, not the marks, under the object; then checks by subtracting the start mark from the end mark

misconceptions.belief: Joins metres and centimetres like digits, writing 1 m 5 cm as 15 cm
signs: Writes 2 m 8 cm as 28 cm
Writes 3 m 40 cm as 340 m
Forgets that the metres part is hundreds of cm

diagnostic.prompt_en: 2 m 8 cm is how many cm?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: 2 m 8 cm kitne cm hain?

remediation.representation: Place-value chart where each metre fills the hundreds column
remediation.moveShape: Child changes the metres to cm first (200), then adds the 8; compare with the joined-up answer on the metre tape

items.prompt_en: A pencil starts at 0 on a ruler and ends at 12. How long is it?
items.prompt_hi: Ek pencil ruler pe 0 se shuru hoti hai aur 12 pe khatam. Woh kitni lambi hai?
items.answer: 12 cm
hints: Where does the pencil start?
From 0, the end mark tells the length.
0 to 12 is ___ cm.
12 cm.

items.prompt_en: How many centimetres make 1 metre?
items.prompt_hi: Kitne centimetre milkar 1 metre bante hain?
hints: Is a metre longer than your hand or shorter?
A metre is 100 small centimetre spaces.
100 cm make 1 metre.

items.prompt_en: 2 m is how many cm?
items.prompt_hi: 2 m kitne cm hain?
items.answer: 200 cm
hints: How many cm in 1 m?
Each metre is 100 cm.

items.prompt_en: A crayon is placed from 3 to 9 on a ruler. Guess: is it 9 cm long or 6 cm long?
items.prompt_hi: Ek crayon ruler pe 3 se 9 tak rakha hai. Guess karo: woh 9 cm lamba hai ya 6 cm?
items.answer: 6 cm
hints: Does the crayon start at 0?
Count the spaces from 3 to 9.
6 cm: from 3 to 9 there are 6 one-cm spaces.

items.prompt_en: Why do we start measuring at 0 and not at 1?
items.prompt_hi: Hum 0 se naapna kyun shuru karte hain, 1 se kyun nahi?
items.answer: Length is the number of 1 cm spaces; from 0 the end mark gives that count; starting at 1 makes the reading 1 cm more than the real length
hints: What does each 1 cm on the ruler stand for?
We count spaces, and the first space starts at 0.
Starting at 1, the end number is ___ more than the length.
From 0 the end reading equals the number of spaces; from 1 it would be 1 cm too much.

items.prompt_en: Which is longer: 1 m or 90 cm?
items.prompt_hi: Kaun lamba hai: 1 m ya 90 cm?
items.answer: 1 m, because 1 m is 100 cm
hints: How many cm is 1 m?
Change both to cm.
100 cm and 90 cm: longer is ___.
1 m is longer: it is 100 cm.

items.prompt_en: 3 m 40 cm is how many cm?
items.prompt_hi: 3 m 40 cm kitne cm hain?
items.answer: 340 cm
hints: How many cm in 3 m?
3 m is 300 cm; add the 40 cm.

items.prompt_en: I wrote 1 m 5 cm = 15 cm. Is that right?
items.prompt_hi: Maine likha 1 m 5 cm = 15 cm. Kya yeh sahi hai?
items.answer: No. 1 m 5 cm = 105 cm
hints: How many cm is the 1 m part?
1 m is 100 cm; then add 5 cm.
No: 1 m 5 cm is 105 cm.

items.prompt_en: Say 150 cm in metres and centimetres.
items.prompt_hi: 150 cm ko metre aur centimetre mein bolo.
items.answer: 1 m 50 cm
hints: How many full 100s are in 150?
Each 100 cm is 1 m; the rest stays as cm.
1 m 50 cm.

items.prompt_en: To make a 2 m long rangoli border, Asha has ribbons that are 50 cm each. How many ribbons does she need?
items.prompt_hi: 2 m lambi rangoli border banane ke liye Asha ke paas 50-50 cm ke ribbon hain. Use kitne ribbon chahiye?
hints: How many cm is 2 m?
2 m is 200 cm; count up in 50s.
4 ribbons: 4 × 50 cm = 200 cm = 2 m.

items.prompt_en: Estimate: is a classroom door about 2 m tall or about 2 cm tall?
items.prompt_hi: Andaaza lagao: class ka darwaza lagbhag 2 m ooncha hai ya 2 cm?
items.answer: About 2 m
hints: Is 2 cm bigger or smaller than your finger?
2 cm is tiny; a door is taller than a grown-up.
A door is about 2 ___.
About 2 m: 2 cm is smaller than a fingernail.

items.prompt_en: The start of Golu's ruler is broken, so it begins at 4. Teach him how to measure a pencil with it.
items.prompt_hi: Golu ki ruler ki shuruaat toot gayi hai, ab woh 4 se shuru hoti hai. Use sikhao isse pencil kaise naapein.
items.answer: Put one end of the pencil at a mark such as 4, read the mark at the other end, and take away 4 (or count the 1 cm spaces between)
hints: Where should Golu put the pencil's end?
Talk about the start mark and the end mark.
Length = end mark − ___.
Line the pencil up at 4, read the end mark and take away 4; that counts the cm spaces.

items.prompt_en: Quick! Half a metre is how many cm?
items.prompt_hi: Jaldi batao! Aadha metre kitne cm hai?
items.answer: 50 cm
hints: How many cm in a whole metre?
Half of 100.
Half of 100 = ___.
50 cm.

workedExample.problem: A stick lies from the 2 mark to the 11 mark on a ruler. How long is it?
steps: The stick does not start at 0, so we cannot just read the end.
End mark is 11 and start mark is 2.
Length = 11 − 2 = 9.
The stick is 9 cm long.
fadedVersion: The stick does not start at ___, so we cannot just read the end.
End mark is ___ and start mark is 2.
The stick is ___ cm long.

skills.title: Find the distance around a shape by adding the lengths of all its sides
Find the distance around rectangles and squares using their equal sides
Tell the distance around a shape apart from the space inside it

expectations: The distance around a shape is the total length of its boundary: add every side
A rectangle has 4 sides, with opposite sides equal: length + width + length + width
A square has 4 equal sides, so the distance around is 4 times one side
Distance around is a length (cm, m, units); the squares inside measure space, which is different

misconceptions.belief: Adds only two sides of a rectangle to find the distance around
signs: Says a 5 cm by 3 cm rectangle has 8 cm around it
Adds the two numbers given and stops
Forgets the sides that were not labelled

diagnostic.prompt_en: A rectangle is 6 cm long and 2 cm wide. What is the distance around it?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek rectangle 6 cm lamba aur 2 cm chauda hai. Uske chaaron taraf ki doori kitni hai?

remediation.representation: An ant walking the boundary, with each side lighting up as it is walked
remediation.moveShape: Child traces all the way round with a finger, saying each side's length aloud, then adds what they said

misconceptions.belief: Counts or multiplies to find the squares inside when asked for the distance around
signs: Counts the inside squares on a grid
Multiplies length by width
Uses 'distance around' and 'space inside' as the same thing

diagnostic.prompt_en: A 2 by 2 square is drawn on a grid. How many units is the distance around it?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Grid pe 2 by 2 ka square bana hai. Uske chaaron taraf ki doori kitni units hai?

remediation.representation: String laid along the boundary, then straightened next to a ruler, beside the same shape filled with tiles
remediation.moveShape: Child measures the straightened string and counts the tiles separately; ask which one is a length and which one is space

misconceptions.belief: Counts the grid squares along the edge instead of the unit lengths, so corners are counted once instead of twice
signs: Says a 3 by 3 square has 8 units around it
Counts squares touching the edge
Gets a total that is 4 short

diagnostic.prompt_en: A 3 by 3 square is drawn on a grid. How many units is the distance around it?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Grid pe 3 by 3 ka square bana hai. Uske chaaron taraf ki doori kitni units hai?

remediation.representation: Grid shape with every unit edge on the boundary coloured, corners showing two coloured edges
remediation.moveShape: Child taps each coloured edge, not each square; ask how many edges a corner square gives

items.prompt_en: A triangle has sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm. What is the distance around it?
items.prompt_hi: Ek triangle ki sides 3 cm, 4 cm aur 5 cm hain. Uske chaaron taraf ki doori kitni hai?
items.answer: 12 cm
hints: How many sides does the triangle have?
Add all three sides.
12 cm.

items.prompt_en: A rectangular table is 2 m long and 1 m wide. What is the distance around it?
items.prompt_hi: Ek rectangle table 2 m lambi aur 1 m chaudi hai. Uske chaaron taraf ki doori kitni hai?
items.answer: 6 m
hints: How many sides does the table top have?
Two long sides and two short sides.

items.prompt_en: A square handkerchief has sides of 20 cm. How much lace is needed for its edge?
items.prompt_hi: Ek square rumaal ki har side 20 cm hai. Uske kinaare ke liye kitni lace chahiye?
items.answer: 80 cm
hints: How many sides does a square have?
All 4 sides are 20 cm.
80 cm of lace.

items.prompt_en: A rectangle is 5 cm by 3 cm. Riya adds 5 + 3 = 8 cm. Guess: will 8 cm of lace go all the way around?
items.prompt_hi: Ek rectangle 5 cm by 3 cm hai. Riya 5 + 3 = 8 cm jodti hai. Guess karo: kya 8 cm lace poore chaaron taraf aa jaayegi?
items.answer: No. It needs 16 cm; she added only two sides
hints: How many sides does a rectangle have?
The other long side and the other short side are missing.
No: 8 cm goes only halfway; all the way around is 16 cm.

items.prompt_en: Why do we add 4 numbers for a rectangle when we are told only 2 lengths?
items.prompt_hi: Rectangle ke liye sirf 2 lambaiyaan di gayi hain, phir bhi hum 4 numbers kyun jodte hain?
items.answer: A rectangle has 4 sides and opposite sides are equal, so the 2 lengths each appear twice
hints: How many sides does a rectangle have?
The side across from the length is the same length.
Length + width + ___ + ___.
It has 4 sides and opposite sides are equal, so we add length + width + length + width.

items.prompt_en: A 3 by 3 square is drawn on a grid. How many small squares are inside it, and how many units is the distance around it?
items.prompt_hi: Grid pe 3 by 3 ka square bana hai. Uske andar kitne chhote squares hain, aur chaaron taraf ki doori kitni units hai?
items.answer: 9 squares inside, 12 units around
hints: Are we counting space or length?
Inside: 3 rows of 3. Around: 4 sides of 3 units.
Inside = ___ squares; around = ___ units.
9 squares inside and 12 units around: two different things.

items.prompt_en: A rectangular garden is 10 m long and 6 m wide. How much fencing is needed to go all around it?
items.prompt_hi: Ek rectangle bageecha 10 m lamba aur 6 m chauda hai. Chaaron taraf kitni baad (fencing) chahiye?
hints: Which sides are the same length?
Two sides of 10 m and two sides of 6 m.
32 m of fencing.

items.prompt_en: A tablecloth is 120 cm long and 80 cm wide. I said the lace needed is 120 + 80 = 200 cm. Am I right?
items.prompt_hi: Ek tablecloth 120 cm lamba aur 80 cm chauda hai. Maine kaha lace chahiye 120 + 80 = 200 cm. Kya main sahi hoon?
items.answer: No. It needs 400 cm, because there are 4 sides
hints: Does 200 cm go all the way around?
Two sides are missing.
No: 400 cm; I added only half the sides.

items.prompt_en: An ant walks along the edge of a rectangle 4 cm by 2 cm, all the way back to where it started. Say its walk as an addition, and give the total.
items.prompt_hi: Ek cheenti 4 cm by 2 cm ke rectangle ke kinaare chalti hai, ghoomkar wahin wapas aati hai. Uski chaal ko addition mein bolo, aur total batao.
hints: Which side does the ant walk first?
It walks every side once.

items.prompt_en: A square park has sides of 50 m. Ramu walks around it 2 times. How far does he walk?
items.prompt_hi: Ek square park ki har side 50 m hai. Ramu uske 2 chakkar lagata hai. Woh kitna chalta hai?
hints: How far is one round?
One round is 4 sides of 50 m.
One round = ___ m; two rounds = ___ m.
400 m: one round is 200 m and he walks two.

items.prompt_en: On a grid, a rectangle is 4 units long and 3 units tall. Meena counted the squares touching the edge, got 10, and said the distance around is 10 units. Is she right?
items.prompt_hi: Grid pe ek rectangle 4 units lamba aur 3 units ooncha hai. Meena ne kinaare ko chhoone wale squares gine, 10 aaye, aur boli chaaron taraf ki doori 10 units hai. Kya woh sahi hai?
items.answer: No. The distance around is 14 units; corner squares each have 2 edges on the boundary
hints: Are we counting squares or edges?
Count the unit edges on the boundary; a corner square gives two.
No: 14 units; counting squares misses one edge at each of the 4 corners.

items.prompt_en: Teach Golu how to find how much lace he needs for the edge of a rectangular tablecloth.
items.prompt_hi: Golu ko sikhao rectangle tablecloth ke kinaare ke liye kitni lace chahiye, kaise nikaalein.
items.answer: Measure the length and width, remember there are 4 sides with opposite sides equal, and add length + width + length + width
hints: What should Golu measure first?
Talk about all 4 sides, not just 2.
Length + width + ___ + ___.
Measure length and width, then add all 4 sides: length + width + length + width.

items.prompt_en: Quick! What does 'distance around a shape' mean?
items.prompt_hi: Jaldi batao! Shape ke 'chaaron taraf ki doori' ka matlab kya hai?
items.answer: The total length of all its sides, its boundary
hints: Think of an ant walking along the edge.
It is a length, not the space inside.
Add up all the ___.
The total length of the boundary: all the sides added.

workedExample.problem: How much lace goes around a rectangular tablecloth 150 cm long and 100 cm wide?
steps: A rectangle has 4 sides and opposite sides are equal.
The sides are 150, 100, 150 and 100 cm.
So 500 cm of lace is needed.
fadedVersion: A rectangle has ___ sides and opposite sides are equal.
The sides are 150, 100, ___ and ___ cm.
So ___ cm of lace is needed.

skills.title: Add 3- and 4-digit numbers with regrouping, lining up the digits by place
Subtract 3- and 4-digit numbers with borrowing, including across zeros
Solve shopping and travel problems by choosing to add or subtract

expectations: Line up ones under ones, tens under tens, hundreds under hundreds, starting from the right
When a column adds to 10 or more, trade 10 of that place for 1 of the next place
In subtraction, always take the bottom digit from the top digit; if the top is smaller, borrow 1 from the next place
Borrowing across a zero: the zero becomes 9 after passing the borrow along
A quick estimate tells whether the answer is sensible

misconceptions.belief: Lines up numbers of different lengths from the left, so digits end up in the wrong places
signs: Writes 48 under the 32 of 3256
Gets a 4-digit total far too big
Adds a 2-digit number to the thousands

diagnostic.prompt_hi: 3402 mein 57 jodo, kitna hua?

remediation.representation: Place-value chart columns with the headings Th, H, T, O over both numbers
remediation.moveShape: Child writes each digit under its heading before adding; ask what the 5 in 57 stands for

misconceptions.belief: In each column takes the smaller digit from the larger one, whichever is on top
signs: Writes 62 − 38 = 36
Never borrows
Answer is bigger than the correct difference

diagnostic.prompt_hi: 62 mein se 38 ghatao, kitna bacha?

remediation.representation: Ten-rods and ones: 6 rods and 2 ones on the mat, take away 3 rods and 8 ones
remediation.moveShape: Child tries to take 8 ones from 2 ones with real blocks and must open a rod; ask where the extra ones came from

misconceptions.belief: Borrows across a zero without changing the zero correctly, or without reducing the place lent from
signs: Treats a zero it borrowed through as 10 instead of 9

diagnostic.prompt_hi: 300 mein se 125 ghatao, kitna bacha?

remediation.representation: Rupee notes: three ₹100 notes, change one for ten ₹10 notes, then one ₹10 for ten ₹1 coins
remediation.moveShape: Child does the trades with play money and writes what is left in each place after each trade; compare with the written borrowing

items.prompt_hi: Chalo jodo: 2345 aur 1432 milake kitna hua?
hints: Which column do we start with?
Add ones, then tens, then hundreds, then thousands.

items.prompt_hi: Ab yeh jodo: 1478 + 2356 kitna hoga? Carry ka dhyaan rakhna.
hints: What do 8 and 6 make in the ones?
8 + 6 = 14: write 4, carry 1 ten.
Tens: 7 + 5 + 1 = 13, write 3, carry 1. Hundreds: 4 + 3 + 1 = ___.

items.prompt_en: Subtract: 5642 − 2318 = ?
items.prompt_hi: Ab ghatao: 5642 mein se 2318 nikaalo, kitna bacha?
hints: Can we take 8 from 2 in the ones?
Borrow 1 ten: 12 − 8 = 4, and 4 tens become 3 tens.
Tens: 3 − 1 = 2. Hundreds: 6 − 3 = ___. Thousands: 5 − 2 = ___.

items.prompt_en: Before adding 3256 + 48, guess: will the answer be close to 3300 or close to 8000?
items.prompt_hi: 3256 + 48 jodne se pehle guess karo: answer 3300 ke paas hoga ya 8000 ke?
items.answer: Close to 3300 (it is 3304)
hints: Is 48 a big number or a small one compared to 3256?
Adding 48 moves us up by less than 100.

items.prompt_en: In 724 − 358, why can't we just do 8 − 4 in the ones place?
items.prompt_hi: 724 − 358 mein, ekai mein seedha 8 − 4 kyun nahi kar sakte?
items.answer: We must take 8 away from 4, because 4 is on top; 4 is less than 8, so we borrow a ten and do 14 − 8 = 6 (answer 366)
hints: Which number are we taking away from?
The top digit is 4; we take the bottom digit 8 from it.
Borrow a ten: 14 − 8 = ___.
Because we take 8 from 4, not 4 from 8; borrow a ten to get 14 − 8 = 6, and 724 − 358 = 366.

items.prompt_en: For 503 − 278, one child got 225 and another got 375. Which is right?
items.prompt_hi: 503 − 278 mein ek bachche ka answer 225 aaya aur doosre ka 375. Kaun sahi hai?
hints: Check: what is 278 + 225?
375 comes from taking the smaller digit from the bigger in each column.
225: 278 + 225 = 503; the 375 came from not borrowing.

items.prompt_en: For a trip, the train ticket costs ₹1250 and the bus ticket costs ₹375. What is the total?
items.prompt_hi: Ek trip ke liye train ticket ₹1250 ka hai aur bus ticket ₹375 ka. Total kitna hua?
hints: Add or subtract for a total?
Line up the ones: 0 and 5.

items.prompt_en: For 4003 − 1256, I wrote 3747. Is that right?
items.prompt_hi: 4003 − 1256 ke liye maine 3747 likha. Kya yeh sahi hai?
items.answer: No. It is 2747; after borrowing, the 4 thousands become 3 thousands and the zeros become 9s
hints: Check: what is 1256 + 3747?
When we borrow from the 4 thousands, it becomes 3 thousands, and each zero passes the borrow along and becomes 9.
Ones 13 − 6 = 7, tens 9 − 5 = 4, hundreds 9 − 2 = 7, thousands 3 − 1 = ___.
No: 2747; I forgot to lower the thousands after borrowing.

items.prompt_en: Show 1365 + 248 with place-value blocks. After trading, how many thousands, hundreds, tens and ones are there?
items.prompt_hi: 1365 + 248 ko place-value blocks se dikhao. Trading ke baad kitne thousands, hundreds, tens aur ones bachte hain?
items.answer: 1 thousand, 6 hundreds, 1 ten, 3 ones: 1613
hints: How many ones are there altogether?
13 ones: trade 10 ones for 1 ten. Then check the tens.
Tens: 6 + 4 + 1 = 11, trade 10 tens for 1 hundred. Hundreds: 3 + 2 + 1 = ___.
1 thousand, 6 hundreds, 1 ten and 3 ones: 1613.

items.prompt_en: Daisy's family travelled 1240 km by train and then 86 km by car to reach Mawlynnong. They came back the same way. How many km did they travel in all?
items.prompt_hi: Daisy ka parivaar Mawlynnong pahunchne ke liye 1240 km train se aur phir 86 km car se gaya. Wapas bhi usi raaste aaye. Kul kitne km safar kiya?
hints: How far is one way?
One way is 1240 + 86; the trip back is the same again.
One way = ___ km; both ways = 1326 + 1326 = ___.
2652 km: 1326 km each way, twice.

items.prompt_en: I added 2508 + 64 by writing the 64 under the 25. I got 8908. Is that right?
items.prompt_hi: Maine 2508 + 64 ko jodte waqt 64 ko 25 ke neeche likha. Answer 8908 aaya. Kya yeh sahi hai?
items.answer: No. It is 2572; the 4 goes under the 8 and the 6 under the 0
hints: Is 64 worth 6 thousand?
Line up from the right: ones under ones.
No: lined up properly, 2508 + 64 = 2572.

items.prompt_en: Teach Golu how to add 3407 + 85 without making a mistake.
items.prompt_hi: Golu ko sikhao 3407 + 85 bina galti ke kaise jodein.
items.answer: Line up from the right (5 under 7, 8 under 0); add ones 7 + 5 = 12, write 2 carry 1; tens 0 + 8 + 1 = 9; hundreds 4; thousands 3: 3492
hints: What should Golu do before adding?
Talk about lining up and carrying.
Ones 7 + 5 = 12, write ___ carry 1; tens 0 + 8 + 1 = ___.
Line up ones under ones, add from the right and carry: 3492.

items.prompt_hi: Jaldi batao! 600 − 250 = ?
hints: What do you add to 250 to make 300?

steps: Line up the numbers by place and start with the ones: 0 − 4 needs a borrow.
The tens and hundreds are 0, so borrow from the thousands: 5 thousands become 4, the hundreds become 9, the tens become 9, and the ones become 10.
Ones 10 − 4 = 6, tens 9 − 3 = 6, hundreds 9 − 8 = 1, thousands 4 − 1 = 3.
fadedVersion: Line up the numbers by place and start with the ___: 0 − 4 needs a borrow.
The tens and hundreds are 0, so borrow from the thousands: 5 thousands become ___, the hundreds become 9, the tens become ___, and the ones become 10.
Ones 10 − 4 = 6, tens 9 − 3 = ___, hundreds 9 − 8 = 1, thousands 4 − 1 = 3.

skills.title: Round prices to estimate a total cost
Decide with an estimate whether an amount of money is enough
Check whether an exact answer is sensible by estimating

expectations: An estimate uses rounded numbers, so it is close to the exact answer but need not be the same
Estimate by rounding each price (to the nearest 10 or 100) and adding the rounded numbers
If every price was rounded up, the real total is less than the estimate; if rounded down, it is more
When the estimate is very close to the money you have, work out the exact total before deciding
An exact answer far from the estimate is a sign of a mistake

misconceptions.belief: Thinks an estimate must be the same as the exact answer, so a close estimate is 'wrong'
signs: Says an estimate of ₹500 is wrong when the exact total is ₹501
Works out the exact answer first and then calls it the estimate
Refuses to estimate 'because it won't be right'

diagnostic.prompt_en: Asha estimated ₹312 + ₹189 as about ₹500. The exact answer is ₹501. Was her estimate wrong?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Asha ne ₹312 + ₹189 ko lagbhag ₹500 socha. Sahi answer ₹501 hai. Kya uska andaaza galat tha?

options.text: No, an estimate only needs to be close

remediation.representation: Number line where the estimate and the exact answer are both marked, close together
remediation.moveShape: Child marks both and measures the gap; ask what an estimate is for (a quick check), and whether this one did its job

misconceptions.belief: Thinks estimating means guessing any number, not rounding and calculating
signs: Says a random number when asked to estimate
Gives estimates far from the real total
Cannot say how they got the estimate

diagnostic.prompt_en: Which is the best way to estimate ₹612 + ₹290?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: ₹612 + ₹290 ka andaaza lagane ka sabse achha tareeka kaunsa hai?

remediation.representation: Rounding number line next to each price tag
remediation.moveShape: Child rounds each price on its own line before adding; ask them to say which hundred each price is nearer to

misconceptions.belief: Believes that if the estimate equals the money you have, the money is surely enough
signs: Says ₹500 is enough because the estimate is ₹500
Does not check which prices were rounded down
Stops at the estimate even when it is right at the limit

diagnostic.prompt_en: You have ₹300. Things cost ₹149 and ₹152. Rounded to the nearest hundred: 100 + 200 = 300. Is ₹300 surely enough?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Tumhare paas ₹300 hain. Cheezein ₹149 aur ₹152 ki hain. Nearest hundred mein: 100 + 200 = 300. Kya ₹300 pakka kaafi hain?

options.text: Not sure, so check the exact total: ₹301, so no

remediation.representation: Price tags with arrows showing which way each was rounded
remediation.moveShape: Child marks each price as rounded up or down, then decides if the real total could be above the money; when it could, work out the exact total

items.prompt_en: A pen costs ₹48. About how much is that, to the nearest ₹10?
items.prompt_hi: Ek pen ₹48 ka hai. Nearest ₹10 mein lagbhag kitna hua?
items.answer: About ₹50
hints: Which two tens is 48 between?
48 is between 40 and 50, and closer to 50.
48 is about ___.
About ₹50.

items.prompt_en: Estimate ₹198 + ₹305 by rounding each to the nearest hundred.
items.prompt_hi: ₹198 + ₹305 ka andaaza lagao, dono ko nearest hundred mein round karke.
items.answer: About ₹500
hints: What is 198 to the nearest hundred?
198 is about 200 and 305 is about 300.
About ₹500.

items.prompt_en: You have ₹500. You want a bag for ₹289 and shoes for ₹195. Estimate: is ₹500 enough?
items.prompt_hi: Tumhare paas ₹500 hain. Tumhe ₹289 ka bag aur ₹195 ke joote chahiye. Andaaza lagao: kya ₹500 kaafi hain?
items.answer: Yes. About 300 + 200 = 500, and both prices were rounded up, so the real total is less (₹484)
hints: Round each price to the nearest hundred.
289 is about 300 and 195 is about 200; both went up.
If both were rounded up, the real total is ___ than 500.
Yes: the estimate is ₹500 and both prices were rounded up, so the real total, ₹484, is less.

items.prompt_en: Before adding ₹412 + ₹289, guess: will the total be about ₹700 or about ₹1000?
items.prompt_hi: ₹412 + ₹289 jodne se pehle guess karo: total lagbhag ₹700 hoga ya ₹1000?
items.answer: About ₹700 (it is ₹701)
hints: What is 412 to the nearest hundred?
412 is about 400 and 289 is about 300.
About ₹700; the exact total is ₹701.

items.prompt_en: You estimated ₹396 + ₹207 as about ₹600, and the exact answer is ₹603. Why are they not the same, and is that okay?
items.prompt_hi: Tumne ₹396 + ₹207 ka andaaza ₹600 lagaya, aur sahi answer ₹603 hai. Dono same kyun nahi hain, aur kya yeh theek hai?
items.answer: The estimate uses rounded numbers (400 and 200), so it is close but not exact; that is fine, because an estimate is a quick check
hints: Which numbers did you use for the estimate?
Rounding changed 396 to 400 and 207 to 200.
An estimate is meant to be ___, not exact.
They differ because the estimate used rounded numbers; being close is exactly what an estimate should do.

items.prompt_en: For ₹478 + ₹205, Rina says 'about ₹700' and Sonu says 'about ₹1200'. Which estimate is sensible, and how do you know?
items.prompt_hi: ₹478 + ₹205 ke liye Rina kehti hai 'lagbhag ₹700' aur Sonu kehta hai 'lagbhag ₹1200'. Kiska andaaza theek hai, aur kaise pata?
items.answer: Rina's: 478 is about 500 and 205 is about 200, so about ₹700 (exact ₹683)
hints: Round each price to the nearest hundred.
478 is about 500; 205 is about 200.
Rina's ₹700 is sensible; ₹1200 is far too big. The exact total is ₹683.

items.prompt_en: Rice costs ₹145, dal ₹98 and sugar ₹42. Estimate the total to the nearest ten. Is ₹300 enough?
items.prompt_hi: Chawal ₹145, daal ₹98 aur chini ₹42 ki hai. Nearest ten mein total ka andaaza lagao. Kya ₹300 kaafi hain?
items.answer: About ₹290, so yes, ₹300 is enough (exact ₹285)
hints: What is each price to the nearest ten?
145 is about 150, 98 about 100, 42 about 40.
About ₹290, so ₹300 is enough; the exact total is ₹285.

items.prompt_en: Nikhil added ₹389 + ₹402 and got ₹1791. He says it looks fine. Use an estimate to check him.
items.prompt_hi: Nikhil ne ₹389 + ₹402 jodkar ₹1791 nikaala. Woh kehta hai theek lagta hai. Andaaze se check karo.
items.answer: Wrong. About 400 + 400 = 800, so ₹1791 is far too big; the exact answer is ₹791
hints: What is each number to the nearest hundred?
389 is about 400 and 402 is about 400.
It is wrong: the estimate is about ₹800, and the exact total is ₹791.

items.prompt_en: Say this bill as a quick estimate, rounding to the nearest ten: chips ₹19, juice ₹31, biscuits ₹48.
items.prompt_hi: Is bill ka jaldi andaaza lagao, nearest ten mein round karke: chips ₹19, juice ₹31, biscuit ₹48.
hints: What is 19 to the nearest ten?
19 is about 20, 31 is about 30, 48 is about 50.
About ₹100; the exact bill is ₹98.

items.prompt_en: A train ticket costs ₹238, food ₹155 and a toy ₹114. Mummy has ₹500. Rounding to the nearest hundred gives 200 + 200 + 100 = ₹500. Is ₹500 surely enough? Find out.
items.prompt_hi: Train ticket ₹238, khaana ₹155 aur ek khilauna ₹114 ka hai. Mummy ke paas ₹500 hain. Nearest hundred mein round karne pe 200 + 200 + 100 = ₹500. Kya ₹500 pakka kaafi hain? Pata karo.
items.answer: No. The estimate is right at the limit, so check the exact total: ₹507, which is ₹7 more than ₹500
hints: Which prices were rounded down?
238 and 114 were rounded down, so the real total could be more than 500.
No: the exact total is ₹507, so ₹500 is ₹7 short.

items.prompt_en: You have ₹200. Two things cost ₹95 and ₹98. Rounding up gives ₹100 + ₹100 = ₹200. Guess: is the real total more or less than ₹200?
items.prompt_hi: Tumhare paas ₹200 hain. Do cheezein ₹95 aur ₹98 ki hain. Upar round karne se ₹100 + ₹100 = ₹200. Guess karo: asli total ₹200 se zyada hai ya kam?
items.answer: Less: both prices were rounded up, so the real total (₹193) is less than ₹200
hints: Did we round the prices up or down?
Both went up, so we added a little extra to each.
Less: ₹193, because both prices were rounded up.

items.prompt_en: Teach Golu how to quickly check if ₹1000 is enough for things costing ₹420, ₹310 and ₹180.
items.prompt_hi: Golu ko sikhao jaldi se kaise check karein ki ₹420, ₹310 aur ₹180 ki cheezon ke liye ₹1000 kaafi hain ya nahi.
items.answer: Round each to the nearest hundred: 400 + 300 + 200 = 900; that is well below ₹1000, so it is enough (exact ₹910)
hints: What should Golu do with each price first?

items.prompt_hi: Ek square ko corner se corner kaata aur ek lambe rectangle ko bhi corner se corner. Dono mein do barabar triangle bane. Kisme dono hisse fold karne pe bilkul ek doosre pe aate hain?
items.answer: The square
hints: Fold each along its cut line. What happens to the corners?
In the square the corners meet; in the rectangle they stick out.
Only the ___ fold matches exactly.
The square: its diagonal is a line of symmetry, the rectangle's is not.

items.prompt_en: Teach Golu how to check whether a shape has a line of symmetry.
items.prompt_hi: Golu ko sikhao kaise check karein ki kisi shape mein symmetry ki line hai ya nahi.
items.answer: Fold the shape along the line (or hold a mirror on it); if one half lies exactly on the other with nothing sticking out, it is a line of symmetry; try other directions too
hints: What should Golu do with the paper?
Talk about folding and checking that nothing sticks out.
Fold; if the halves match ___, it is a line of symmetry; then try ___ folds.
Fold along the line; if the halves match exactly it is a line of symmetry; then try folding other ways too.

items.prompt_en: Quick! How many lines of symmetry does a circle have?
items.prompt_hi: Jaldi batao! Circle mein symmetry ki kitni lines hoti hain?
items.answer: Endless (very many)
hints: Does every fold through the centre work?
Any line through the centre folds a circle onto itself.
There are ___ lines.
Endless: every line through the centre works.

workedExample.problem: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle (not a square) have?
steps: Fold it top to bottom: the halves match, so that is one line.
Fold it side to side: the halves match, so that is a second line.
Fold it corner to corner: two corners stick out, so that is not a line of symmetry.
So a rectangle has 2 lines of symmetry.
fadedVersion: Fold it top to bottom: the halves ___, so that is one line.
Fold it side to side: the halves match, so that is a ___ line.
Fold it corner to corner: two corners stick ___, so that is not a line of symmetry.
So a rectangle has ___ lines of symmetry.

skills.title: Complete a figure across a standing mirror line by flipping its half
Put each mirror point the same distance from the line on the other side
Complete figures across a lying line, or across two lines in a rangoli

expectations: The missing half is a flip of the given half, not a copy slid across
Each point goes the same number of squares from the mirror line, on the other side, straight across
With a standing line, points move left or right only; with a lying line, up or down only
A point on the mirror line stays where it is

misconceptions.belief: Copies the half and slides it across without flipping it
signs: Draws the second wing facing the same way as the first
An arrow pointing left stays pointing left
The completed figure looks lopsided

diagnostic.prompt_en: Half of a figure has a flag pointing left, away from a standing mirror line. In the completed figure, the other flag points…
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek aadhi figure mein jhanda left ki taraf hai, standing mirror line se door. Poori figure mein doosra jhanda kis taraf hoga…

remediation.representation: A mirror held on the line, or a paper folded and pricked through with a pin
remediation.moveShape: Child predicts, then checks with a real mirror or a folded paper; ask which way the reflection faces compared to the original

misconceptions.belief: Places the mirror point at a different distance from the line
signs: Puts the reflection at the edge of the paper
Counts squares from the paper's edge instead of from the line
The completed figure is stretched or squashed

diagnostic.prompt_en: A dot is 3 squares to the left of the mirror line. Where is its mirror dot?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek dot mirror line se 3 square left mein hai. Uska mirror dot kahan hoga?

options.text: 3 squares to the right of the line
At the right edge of the paper
1 square to the right of the line

remediation.representation: Grid with the squares counted out loud from the mirror line on both sides
remediation.moveShape: Child counts squares from the line to the dot, then counts the same number on the other side; ask where the counting starts

misconceptions.belief: Reflects in the wrong direction, for example moves a point up or down when the mirror line is standing
signs: Flips top to bottom across a standing line
Puts a top-left flower at the bottom-right
Reflects diagonally

diagnostic.prompt_en: The mirror line is standing. A dot is at the top left. Where is its mirror dot?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Mirror line khadi hai. Ek dot upar left mein hai. Uska mirror dot kahan hoga?

remediation.representation: Fold along the line and prick the dot through both layers
remediation.moveShape: Child folds along the actual line and pricks through; ask which way the dot travelled: across, or up and down

items.prompt_en: A dot is 2 squares to the left of a standing mirror line. Where does its mirror dot go?
items.prompt_hi: Ek dot khadi mirror line se 2 square left mein hai. Uska mirror dot kahan jaayega?
items.answer: 2 squares to the right of the line
hints: How far is the dot from the line?
The mirror dot is just as far on the other side.
2 squares to the ___ of the line.
2 squares to the right of the line, in the same row.

items.prompt_en: Half a butterfly is drawn: only the left wing, touching a standing mirror line. How must the right wing be drawn?
items.prompt_hi: Aadhi titli bani hai: sirf left wala pankh, jo khadi mirror line ko chhoo raha hai. Right wala pankh kaise banana hai?
items.answer: The same size and shape, but flipped so it faces the other way, touching the line at the same places
hints: If you folded the paper on the line, where would the left wing land?
The right wing is the mirror image of the left wing.
Same size and shape, but ___.
Flipped: the right wing is the same size and shape as the left, facing the other way.

items.prompt_en: A point is 4 squares to the right of a standing mirror line, in the bottom row. Where is its mirror point?
items.prompt_hi: Ek point khadi mirror line se 4 square right mein hai, sabse neeche wali row mein. Uska mirror point kahan hai?
items.answer: 4 squares to the left of the line, in the bottom row
hints: Does the row change when we reflect across a standing line?
Only the side changes; the row and the distance stay the same.
4 squares to the ___, in the ___ row.
4 squares to the left of the line, still in the bottom row.

items.prompt_en: An arrow points to the left, away from a standing mirror line. Guess: in the mirror half, which way will the arrow point?
items.prompt_hi: Ek arrow left ki taraf hai, khadi mirror line se door. Guess karo: mirror wale hisse mein arrow kis taraf hoga?
items.answer: To the right, away from the line
hints: When you look in a mirror and point away from it, which way does your reflection point?
A mirror flips left and right across a standing line.
The mirror arrow points to the ___.
To the right: it also points away from the line, so it faces the other way.

items.prompt_en: Why must a mirror dot be the same number of squares from the line as the original dot?
items.prompt_hi: Mirror dot, asli dot jitne hi square line se door kyun hona chahiye?
items.answer: Folding along the line puts each dot exactly on top of its mirror dot, so both must be the same distance from the line
hints: What happens to the two dots if you fold along the line?
They must land on top of each other.
When folded they ___, so the distances are equal.
Folding on the line brings each dot onto its mirror dot, which only works if both are equally far from the line.

items.prompt_en: Half of a rangoli has a flower at the top left, near a standing mirror line. Ria draws its mirror at the top right, near the line. Sam draws it at the bottom right. Who is right?
items.prompt_hi: Rangoli ke aadhe hisse mein upar left, khadi mirror line ke paas, ek phool hai. Ria uska mirror upar right, line ke paas banati hai. Sam neeche right banata hai. Kaun sahi hai?
items.answer: Ria
hints: With a standing line, does the flower move up or down?
It moves straight across, staying at the same height.
Top left reflects to top ___.
Ria is right: across a standing line the flower stays at the top and moves to the right.

items.prompt_en: Now the mirror line is lying flat. A dot is 3 squares above it. Where does its mirror dot go?
items.prompt_hi: Ab mirror line leti hui hai. Ek dot usse 3 square upar hai. Uska mirror dot kahan jaayega?
items.answer: 3 squares below the line, straight down
hints: With a lying line, does the dot move sideways or up and down?
It goes straight across the line, the same distance.
3 squares ___ the line.
3 squares below the line, straight down.

items.prompt_en: A dot is 1 square to the left of the line. I drew its mirror 3 squares to the right. Is that right?
items.prompt_hi: Ek dot line se 1 square left mein hai. Maine uska mirror 3 square right mein banaya. Kya yeh sahi hai?
items.answer: No. It should be 1 square to the right
hints: How far is the first dot from the line?
The mirror dot is the same distance away.
1 square left means ___ square right.
No: the mirror dot goes 1 square to the right.

items.prompt_en: Only the left half of a capital A and the middle mirror line are shown. Say in words how to complete it.
items.prompt_hi: Capital A ka sirf left wala aadha hissa aur beech ki mirror line dikh rahi hai. Shabdon mein batao ise kaise poora karein.
items.answer: Draw a slanting line from the top down to the right, the mirror of the left side, and finish the other half of the crossbar the same length
hints: Which way does the left side slant?
The right side slants the opposite way, from the same top point.
Slant down to the ___, and finish the ___.
From the top, slant down to the right like a mirror of the left side, and complete the crossbar.

items.prompt_en: A rangoli has a standing line and a lying line of symmetry. One diya is drawn in the top-left part. How many diyas will the complete rangoli have, and where?
items.prompt_hi: Ek rangoli mein symmetry ki ek khadi line aur ek leti line hai. Upar-left hisse mein ek diya bana hai. Poori rangoli mein kitne diye honge, aur kahan?
items.answer: 4: top-left, top-right, bottom-left and bottom-right
hints: Across the standing line, where does the diya go?
Reflect across the standing line, then reflect both diyas across the lying line.
2 at the top, then ___ at the bottom: ___ in all.
4 diyas, one in each corner part: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right.

items.prompt_en: To complete a heart from its left half, Ravi copied the same half and slid it to the right without flipping it. Will it make a heart?
items.prompt_hi: Dil ka left wala aadha hissa poora karne ke liye Ravi ne wahi hissa copy karke bina palte right mein khiska diya. Kya dil banega?
items.answer: No. The half must be flipped; slid across, its curves face the wrong way
hints: Which way does the bump of the left half face?
The right half must be its mirror image.
Slid without flipping, the bump faces the ___ way.
No: it must be flipped so the curves face the other way; sliding makes a lopsided shape.

items.prompt_en: Teach Golu how to complete half a picture on a grid across a mirror line.
items.prompt_hi: Golu ko sikhao grid pe mirror line ke paar aadhi picture kaise poori karein.
items.answer: Pick a corner point, count squares from it to the mirror line, count the same number on the other side straight across, mark it; do this for every corner point and join them; points on the line stay put
acceptable: same distance on the other side
hints: What should Golu count first?
Talk about counting from the line and going straight across.
Count from the point to the ___, then the same number on the other side.
For each corner point, count squares to the line and the same number past it; mark and join the points.

items.prompt_en: Quick! A dot is ON the mirror line. Where is its mirror dot?
items.prompt_hi: Jaldi batao! Ek dot mirror line ke UPAR hi hai. Uska mirror dot kahan hai?
items.answer: In the same place, on the line
hints: How far is the dot from the line?
0 squares away means it stays put.
It stays ___.
In the same place: a point on the line is its own mirror point.

workedExample.problem: Complete the mirror image of a dot that is 3 squares left of a standing mirror line, in row 2.
steps: Count from the dot to the mirror line: 3 squares.
With a standing line, the mirror dot stays in the same row, row 2.
Count 3 squares to the right of the line.
Mark the mirror dot there: 3 squares right of the line, in row 2.
fadedVersion: Count from the dot to the mirror line: ___ squares.
With a standing line, the mirror dot stays in the same ___, row 2.
Count 3 squares to the ___ of the line.
Mark the mirror dot there: ___ squares right of the line, in row 2.

skills.title: Read a clock to the nearest 5 minutes
Use a.m. for times from midnight to noon and p.m. for times from noon to midnight
Read times on timetables such as a railway board

expectations: The short hand shows the hour; the long hand shows the minutes
The minute hand counts by 5s: on 1 it is 5 minutes, on 4 it is 20 minutes, on 9 it is 45 minutes
The hour is the number the short hand has just passed, not the one it is coming to
a.m. is from midnight to noon and p.m. is from noon to midnight, so 12 noon is 12 p.m.

misconceptions.belief: Thinks 12 noon is 12 a.m.
signs: Writes lunch at 12 a.m.
Says a.m. means 'daytime'
Is unsure about times between 12 and 1

diagnostic.prompt_en: What is 12 o'clock in the daytime (noon) called?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Din ke 12 baje (dopahar) ko kya kehte hain?

remediation.representation: A day-strip from midnight to midnight with a.m. and p.m. shaded in two colours
remediation.moveShape: Child places their day's events on the strip; ask which colour lunch at 12 sits on and what changes at noon

misconceptions.belief: Reads the number the minute hand points to as the minutes (hand on 4 read as 4 minutes)
signs: Reads 10:25 as 10:05
Says 'minute hand on 6 means 6 minutes'
Does not count by 5s

diagnostic.prompt_en: The minute hand is on 6 and the hour hand is halfway between 3 and 4. What time is it?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Minute ki sui 6 pe hai aur ghante ki sui 3 aur 4 ke beech mein. Kya time hua?

remediation.representation: Clock face with a ring of minute labels 5, 10, 15, … outside the hour numbers
remediation.moveShape: Child counts by 5s around to the minute hand, touching each number; then hide the ring and repeat

misconceptions.belief: Reads the hour as the next number when the hour hand is close to it
signs: Reads 2:45 as 3:45
Says the hour from whichever number the short hand is nearest
Times are an hour late

diagnostic.prompt_en: The minute hand is on 10 and the hour hand is nearly at 6. What time is it?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Minute ki sui 10 pe hai aur ghante ki sui lagbhag 6 pe. Kya time hua?

remediation.representation: Geared clock where moving the minute hand drags the hour hand slowly
remediation.moveShape: Child turns the minute hand from 5:00 towards 6:00 and watches the hour hand creep; ask when the hour hand actually reaches 6

items.prompt_en: The minute hand points to 3. How many minutes past the hour is it?
items.prompt_hi: Minute ki sui 3 pe hai. Ghante ke baad kitne minute hue?
items.answer: 15 minutes
hints: How many minutes is each number for the minute hand?
Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15.
15 minutes past.

items.prompt_en: The hour hand is just past 7 and the minute hand points to 4. What time is it?
items.prompt_hi: Ghante ki sui 7 se thoda aage hai aur minute ki sui 4 pe. Kya time hua?
hints: Which hour has the short hand just passed?
The minute hand on 4 means 4 × 5 minutes.

items.prompt_en: School starts at 8 in the morning. Is that 8 a.m. or 8 p.m.?
items.prompt_hi: School subah 8 baje shuru hota hai. Woh 8 a.m. hai ya 8 p.m.?
items.answer: 8 a.m.
hints: Is the morning before noon or after noon?
a.m. is from midnight to noon.
Morning times are ___.
8 a.m., because it is before noon.

items.prompt_en: The minute hand is on 9 and the hour hand is between 2 and 3, close to 3. Guess: is it 3:45 or 2:45?
items.prompt_hi: Minute ki sui 9 pe hai aur ghante ki sui 2 aur 3 ke beech, 3 ke paas. Guess karo: 3:45 hai ya 2:45?
hints: Has the hour hand reached 3 yet?
The hour is the number the short hand has passed.
It has passed ___, so it is ___:45.
2:45: the hour hand has not reached 3 yet.

items.prompt_en: You said the minute hand on 8 means 40 minutes. Why not 8 minutes?
items.prompt_hi: Tumne kaha minute ki sui 8 pe matlab 40 minute. 8 minute kyun nahi?
items.answer: For the minute hand, each number is 5 minutes after the one before, so 8 numbers is 8 × 5 = 40 minutes
hints: How many minutes between 12 and 1 for the minute hand?
There are 5 small minute marks between each number.
Each number is 5 minutes for the minute hand, so 8 means 40 minutes.

items.prompt_en: 12 noon and 12 midnight: which one is 12 p.m. and which one is 12 a.m.?
items.prompt_hi: Dopahar 12 baje aur aadhi raat 12 baje: kaunsa 12 p.m. hai aur kaunsa 12 a.m.?
items.answer: 12 noon is 12 p.m. and 12 midnight is 12 a.m.
hints: What starts at noon, a.m. or p.m.?
p.m. starts at noon; a.m. starts at midnight.
Noon = 12 ___; midnight = 12 ___.
12 noon is 12 p.m. and 12 midnight is 12 a.m.

items.prompt_en: A railway board says a train leaves at 6:35 p.m. Is that in the morning or in the evening? Where will the minute hand be?
items.prompt_hi: Railway board pe likha hai train 6:35 p.m. pe chhootegi. Woh subah hai ya shaam? Minute ki sui kahan hogi?
items.answer: In the evening; the minute hand will be on 7
hints: Is p.m. before or after noon?
35 minutes is 7 jumps of 5.
p.m. after noon means ___; 35 ÷ 5 = ___.
Evening, and the minute hand is on 7.

items.prompt_en: The minute hand is on 5 and the hour hand is just past 10. I say it is 10:05. Am I right?
items.prompt_hi: Minute ki sui 5 pe hai aur ghante ki sui 10 se thoda aage. Main kehta hoon 10:05 hue. Kya main sahi hoon?
items.answer: No. It is 10:25, because the minute hand on 5 means 25 minutes
hints: How many minutes does the 5 stand for?
Count by 5s up to the 5: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25.
No: it is 10:25.

items.prompt_en: Tell me where both hands are at 4:30.
items.prompt_hi: Batao 4:30 baje dono suiyan kahan hongi.
items.answer: The minute hand is on 6; the hour hand is halfway between 4 and 5
hints: 30 minutes is how many jumps of 5?
The minute hand is on 6; the hour hand has moved half the way to 5.
Minute hand on ___; hour hand halfway between 4 and ___.
Minute hand on 6, hour hand halfway between 4 and 5.

items.prompt_en: Ravi says, 'Let's meet at 7 o'clock.' What could go wrong if he does not say a.m. or p.m.?
items.prompt_hi: Ravi kehta hai, 'Chalo 7 baje milte hain.' Agar woh a.m. ya p.m. na bole, toh kya gadbad ho sakti hai?
items.answer: His friend might come at 7 in the morning instead of 7 in the evening; a.m. or p.m. tells which half of the day
hints: How many times does the clock show 7 in one day?
7 comes once in the morning and once in the evening.
a.m. or p.m. tells us which ___ of the day.
There are two 7 o'clocks in a day; without a.m. or p.m. his friend might come at the wrong one.

items.prompt_en: Clock A: minute hand on 2, hour hand just past 11. Clock B: minute hand on 11, hour hand almost at 3. Which shows 11:10 and which shows 2:55?
items.prompt_hi: Ghadi A: minute ki sui 2 pe, ghante ki sui 11 se thoda aage. Ghadi B: minute ki sui 11 pe, ghante ki sui lagbhag 3 pe. Kaun 11:10 dikha rahi hai aur kaun 2:55?
items.answer: Clock A shows 11:10 and clock B shows 2:55
hints: Which hand tells the hour in each clock?
Minute hand on 2 is 10 minutes; on 11 is 55 minutes.
A shows 11:10; B shows 2:55, because its hour hand has not reached 3.

items.prompt_en: Teach Golu how to read the time when the minute hand is on 7.
items.prompt_hi: Golu ko sikhao jab minute ki sui 7 pe ho toh time kaise padhein.
items.answer: Count by 5s up to the 7 (5, 10, … 35): 35 minutes; then read the hour from the number the short hand has just passed
hints: What should Golu count?
Talk about counting by 5s and reading the short hand.
7 × 5 = ___ minutes; the hour is the number the short hand has ___.
Count 5s up to 7 to get 35 minutes, then say the hour the short hand has just passed.

items.prompt_en: Quick! Lunch at 1 o'clock in the afternoon: a.m. or p.m.?
items.prompt_hi: Jaldi batao! Dopahar 1 baje ka khaana: a.m. ya p.m.?
items.answer: p.m.
hints: Is 1 o'clock in the afternoon before or after noon?
After noon is p.m.
1 o'clock in the afternoon is 1 ___.
1 p.m.

workedExample.problem: Read the clock: the hour hand is just past 9 and the minute hand is on 11.
steps: The short hand has just passed 9, so the hour is 9.
The long hand is on 11; count by 5s: 5, 10, 15 … up to 11 numbers.
11 × 5 = 55 minutes.
So the time is 9:55.
fadedVersion: The short hand has just passed ___, so the hour is 9.
The long hand is on 11; count by ___: 5, 10, 15 … up to 11 numbers.
11 × 5 = ___ minutes.
So the time is ___.

skills.title: Find how long an activity takes by counting on from the start time to the end time
Change minutes beyond 60 into hours and minutes
Count days and weeks on a calendar

expectations: Count on from the start: first to the next full hour, then whole hours, then the extra minutes
60 minutes make 1 hour, so a clock never shows more than 59 minutes
Time is not like ordinary numbers: 2:10 − 1:50 is 20 minutes, not 60
Counting days ahead: start counting from the day after today; a week is 7 days

misconceptions.belief: Adds minutes beyond 60 without changing them into an hour
signs: Writes 1:50 + 20 minutes as 1:70
Says 80 minutes is 8 hours
Writes times like 3:75

diagnostic.prompt_en: It is 3:45. What time will it be in 30 minutes?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Abhi 3:45 hue hain. 30 minute baad kya time hoga?

remediation.representation: Geared clock where the hour hand moves on when the minute hand passes 12
remediation.moveShape: Child moves the minute hand round 30 minutes and watches it pass 12; ask what happened to the hour

misconceptions.belief: Subtracts times as if they were ordinary numbers (2:10 − 1:50 as 210 − 150 = 60)
signs: Says 4:50 to 5:10 is 60 minutes
Borrows 100 instead of 60
Gets elapsed times that are too long

diagnostic.prompt_en: How long is it from 4:50 to 5:10?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: 4:50 se 5:10 tak kitna samay hua?

remediation.representation: Time number line with the hour mark 5:00 drawn as a stepping stone
remediation.moveShape: Child jumps from 4:50 to 5:00, then from 5:00 to 5:10, and adds the two jumps

misconceptions.belief: Counts the starting day as one of the days ahead
signs: Says from the 4th to the 11th is 8 days
Says 'today is one'
Answers are one day too many

diagnostic.prompt_en: Monday is the 1st and Thursday is the 4th. How many days after Monday is Thursday?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Monday 1 tareekh hai aur Thursday 4 tareekh. Monday ke kitne din baad Thursday hai?

remediation.representation: Calendar where each hop to the next date is drawn as an arrow
remediation.moveShape: Child counts arrows (hops), not boxes; ask whether they moved when they said 'one' on the start day

items.prompt_en: Cricket practice starts at 4:00 p.m. and ends at 6:00 p.m. How long is it?
items.prompt_hi: Cricket practice shaam 4:00 baje shuru hoti hai aur 6:00 baje khatam. Kitni der chali?
items.answer: 2 hours
hints: How many hours from 4 to 5?
4 to 5 is one hour, 5 to 6 is another.
2 hours.

items.prompt_en: 80 minutes is how many hours and minutes?
items.prompt_hi: 80 minute kitne ghante aur minute hue?
items.answer: 1 hour 20 minutes
hints: How many minutes make an hour?
Take 60 minutes out to make 1 hour.
80 − 60 = ___ minutes left.
1 hour 20 minutes.

items.prompt_en: A movie starts at 3:30 p.m. and ends at 5:15 p.m. How long is it?
items.prompt_hi: Ek movie 3:30 p.m. pe shuru hoti hai aur 5:15 p.m. pe khatam. Movie kitni lambi hai?
items.answer: 1 hour 45 minutes
hints: How long from 3:30 to 4:00?
3:30 to 4:00 is 30 minutes; 4:00 to 5:00 is 1 hour; 5:00 to 5:15 is 15 minutes.
30 + 15 = ___ minutes, plus 1 hour.
1 hour 45 minutes.

items.prompt_en: It is 1:50 and a 20-minute game starts now. Guess: will it end at 1:70 or at 2:10?
items.prompt_hi: Abhi 1:50 hue hain aur 20 minute ka khel shuru hota hai. Guess karo: woh 1:70 pe khatam hoga ya 2:10 pe?
hints: How many minutes from 1:50 to 2:00?
10 minutes gets to 2:00; 10 more minutes are left.
2:10: a clock never shows 70 minutes.

items.prompt_en: Why can a clock never show 1:70?
items.prompt_hi: Ghadi kabhi 1:70 kyun nahi dikha sakti?
items.answer: After 59 minutes a new hour starts, because 60 minutes make 1 hour; 1:70 would really be 2:10
hints: What happens when the minute hand reaches 12 again?
60 minutes make 1 hour, so the hour moves on.
1:70 is really ___.
60 minutes make an hour, so after 1:59 comes 2:00; 1:70 would be 2:10.

items.prompt_en: Way A: 2:10 − 1:50 = 60 minutes, by doing 210 − 150. Way B: from 1:50 to 2:00 is 10 minutes, and from 2:00 to 2:10 is 10 more, so 20 minutes. Which way is right?
items.prompt_hi: Tareeka A: 2:10 − 1:50 = 60 minute, 210 − 150 karke. Tareeka B: 1:50 se 2:00 tak 10 minute, aur 2:00 se 2:10 tak 10 aur, toh 20 minute. Kaunsa tareeka sahi hai?
items.answer: Way B: 20 minutes
hints: How many minutes are in an hour, 60 or 100?
Way A treats an hour as 100 minutes.
10 + 10 = ___ minutes.
Way B is right: 20 minutes, because an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.

items.prompt_en: A bus leaves at 10:45 a.m. and reaches at 1:15 p.m. How long is the journey?
items.prompt_hi: Ek bus 10:45 a.m. pe chalti hai aur 1:15 p.m. pe pahunchti hai. Safar kitna lamba hai?
items.answer: 2 hours 30 minutes
hints: How long from 10:45 to 11:00?
15 minutes, then 11:00 to 1:00 is 2 hours, then 15 more minutes.
15 + 15 = ___ minutes, plus 2 hours.
2 hours 30 minutes.

items.prompt_en: Today is the 4th and my birthday is on the 11th. I counted 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 and said 8 days to go. Am I right?
items.prompt_hi: Aaj 4 tareekh hai aur mera birthday 11 ko hai. Maine gina 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 aur kaha 8 din baaki hain. Kya main sahi hoon?
items.answer: No. It is 7 days; today should not be counted
hints: Does a day 'go by' when you say today's date?
Start counting from tomorrow, the 5th.
No: 7 days to go, because today is not counted.

items.prompt_en: On a calendar, Monday is the 2nd. What is the date two Mondays later?
items.prompt_hi: Calendar pe Monday 2 tareekh ko hai. Do Monday baad kaunsi tareekh hogi?
items.answer: The 16th
hints: What is the date one Monday later?
Each Monday later adds 7 days.
The 16th.

items.prompt_en: Suppose a Rajdhani train leaves Delhi at 4:55 p.m. and reaches the next morning at 8:55 a.m. How long is the journey?
items.prompt_hi: Maan lo ek Rajdhani train Delhi se 4:55 p.m. pe chalti hai aur agli subah 8:55 a.m. pe pahunchti hai. Safar kitni der ka hai?
items.answer: 16 hours
hints: How long from 4:55 p.m. to 4:55 a.m.?
4:55 p.m. to 4:55 a.m. is 12 hours; then on to 8:55 a.m.
16 hours: 12 hours to 4:55 a.m. and 4 more to 8:55 a.m.

items.prompt_en: A school camp lasts 3 weeks and 2 days. How many days is that?
items.prompt_hi: Ek school camp 3 hafte aur 2 din chalta hai. Kitne din hue?
items.answer: 23 days
hints: How many days are in 1 week?
3 weeks is 3 × 7 days; then add 2.
23 days.

items.prompt_en: Teach Golu how to find how long it is from 9:40 a.m. to 11:10 a.m.
items.prompt_hi: Golu ko sikhao 9:40 a.m. se 11:10 a.m. tak kitna samay hai, kaise nikaalein.
items.answer: Count on: 9:40 to 10:00 is 20 minutes, 10:00 to 11:00 is 1 hour, 11:00 to 11:10 is 10 minutes; in all 1 hour 30 minutes
hints: Where should Golu jump to first?
Talk about jumping to the next full hour, then whole hours, then minutes.
20 minutes + 1 hour + 10 minutes = ___.

items.prompt_en: Quick! 90 minutes is how many hours and minutes?
items.prompt_hi: Jaldi batao! 90 minute kitne ghante aur minute hain?
items.answer: 1 hour 30 minutes
hints: Take out 60 minutes. How many are left?
60 minutes is 1 hour.
1 hour 30 minutes.

workedExample.problem: A bus leaves at 8:45 a.m. and arrives at 11:20 a.m. How long is the journey?
steps: Jump to the next full hour: 8:45 to 9:00 is 15 minutes.

Jump the extra minutes: 11:00 to 11:20 is 20 minutes.

items.prompt_hi: Train ke ek coach mein 72 seat hain. 10 coach mein kitni seat hongi?

10 coaches of 72 is 72 × 10.
720 seats.

3 groups of 34 can be broken into 3 groups of 30 and 3 groups of 4.

items.prompt_hi: Ek bus mein 46 seat hain. 5 bus mein kitni seat hongi?
hints: Split 46 into tens and ones.
230 seats.

One part is 10 × 4 and the other is 6 × 4.
40 and 24, which make 64.

items.prompt_en: The transport museum has 125 toy cars on each shelf. There are 6 shelves. How many toy cars are there?

750 toy cars.

items.prompt_en: What is 214 × 3?
items.prompt_hi: 214 guna 3 kitna hoga?

Multiply each part by 3.

items.prompt_en: Teach Golu how to multiply 43 × 6.
items.prompt_hi: Golu ko sikhao 43 × 6 kaise karte hain.
items.answer: Split 43 into 40 and 3; 40 × 6 = 240 and 3 × 6 = 18; add them: 258
hints: What should Golu split 43 into?
Talk about multiplying both parts and adding.
Split into 40 and 3: 240 + 18 = 258.

hints: Share the 8 tens first. How many tens each?
8 tens shared by 4 is 2 tens each; 4 ones shared by 4 is 1 each.
2 tens and 1 one = ___.
21 tickets each.

items.prompt_hi: 72 ko 4 se bhaag do, kitna aaya?

30 + 2 = 32 ones, shared by 4 = ___ each.
18: 1 ten and 8 ones each. Check: 4 × 18 = 72.
